title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Mondays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Belly Dancing with Raja - Tuesdays
description:
DATE AND TIME: Tuesdays @ 11:00 AM

Unlock your inner strength and find your flow. Belly dancing with Raja is an innovative fusion class that blends the rhythmic artistry of belly dance with the high-energy benefits of aerobics. Designed to be both a cardiovascular challenge and a deep toning session, this class focuses on the “powerhouse” of the body—your core.

By layering fluid, isolative movements over an athletic aerobic base, you will challenge your muscles in ways traditional gym workouts can’t reach.

What to Expect in Belly Dancing Class

• Core-Centric Power: Use undulations and shimmies to engage deep abdominal muscles for a tighter, stronger midsection.

• Functional Stability: Improve your balance and posture through controlled, hip-driven movements and low-impact aerobic footwork.

• Total Body Toning: Build lean muscle in your legs, glutes, and arms while maintaining a constant, heart-pumping pace.

• Mind-Body Connection: Enhance your coordination and body awareness through rhythmic, expressive choreography.

“Whether you’re looking to define your waistline or simply want a workout that feels like a celebration, this class offers the perfect balance of sweat and grace.”

Difficulty Level: All levels welcome! No prior dance experience is required—just bring your energy and a willingness to move.

description:

No matter how much we achieve, something within us still asks: “Is this it? Isn’t there something more?”

The Kabbalah of Meaning is a new six-session JLI course exploring the Jewish answer to that question. What are we really searching for—and where can it be found?

Drawing on Kabbalah and centuries of Jewish wisdom, we’ll uncover the essential building blocks of a deeply meaningful life. We’ll explore how purpose can be found in our work, relationships, challenges, accomplishments, and even the ordinary routines that fill our days.

You don’t have to revamp your life. You don’t need to meditate on a mountaintop. You simply need a new lens through which to see the rich world of meaning already woven into every part of your life.

Thoughtful, practical, and surprisingly relevant, this course offers fresh perspectives and useful tools for living with greater clarity, connection, and intention.

description:
Rosicrucians AMORC, Santa Rosa, CA
Rosicrucian Open Meeting. The public is welcome to attend.

**Progress and Inner Development**

Written by: Robert E. Daniels, F.R.C., for the *Rosicrucian Beacon,* June 2009

In this article, the author describes how the Rosicrucian system of study has three phases, the study of our physical nature followed by the intellectual comprehension of Rosicrucian philosophy. Finally, Frater Daniels details how the purpose of the third emotional phase is to develop our awareness of the inner, hidden parts of our being, the so-called “psychic self,” where we become more sensitive to our universe. This is also the most difficult phase for students on the mystical path because we have no yardstick to measure our progress and after some time and study we come to the realization that the process is not a short one but ultimately one that provides great joy and deeper compassion for others.

Presented by Dan Villalva, F.R.C., Secretary for the Santa Rosa Pronaos.
All are invited to attend this lecture and discussion.

About the Santa Rosa Pronaos
We hold a monthly public presentation on mystical or metaphysical topics as a public service. The topics and speakers vary and no previous knowledge or experience is required. Just bring an open mind and heart.

The Santa Rosa Pronaos doesn't charge for admission. As always, our events are free, and donations are gratefully accepted to help defray our costs.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

FSVAA proudly presents the 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show at the Solano Town Center Gallery – show opening is Friday, Nov 13. Gallery Hours are Wed thru Sun, 11am–6pm.

 The three jurors, Ferdinanda Florence, Nadja Fitchhorn, and Vickie Marchand have spoken and made their selections!

We received 200 art entries from 67 talented artists representing 15 different cities throughout Northern California, making this an exciting and impressive year for our Juried Art Show.

It was wonderful to see so many artists arrive with their treasured works of art, eager to have them reviewed and considered by our three distinguished jurors.

After careful deliberation, the jurors selected 97 outstanding works of art to be included in this year's Juried Art Show!

Congratulations to all the artists whose work was selected, and thank you to everyone who participated and helped make this year's show such a success.

title: Coordinated Entry Advisory Committee Meeting December 2, 2026
S.R. Laws
description:
S.R. LAWS IS OUT THERE: He approaches songwriting with a passion for songs that we all grew up on. His sound rings a familiar bell in your head while still delivering ideas completely unique.  He draws inspiration from outstanding storytellers like John Hiatt, Lou Reed, Steve Earle, Neil Finn and Ron Sexsmith. All of their music and others have carved a deep groove. 

Growing up out there in Northern California, he developed a unique connection to music early on. His father worked as a trash collector, and he would spend hours sifting through bags of discarded 45 records. Each find felt like stumbling upon hidden treasures. Some records were covered in dirt and grime, while others were pristine. The thrill of discovering new sounds was exhilarating, and he could hardly wait to drop the needle and immerse himself in the music.

He embarked on a pilgrimage to Texas with just two suitcases and $500 in his bank account. His goal was to dive into the vibrant music scene and learn from fellow songwriters. Austin, known as the "Live Music Capital of the World," offered countless opportunities for him to grow as an artist. Open mics and songwriters' nights became his training ground, where he soaked up every moment, listening to others share their stories through music.

These days, he resides in Sonoma County, California, working hard as a touring artist and singer-songwriter for his original rock band, The Heartsleeves. He invites everyone to join him on this musical journey, sharing his songs one person at a time in this vast and unpredictable world we live in.

“Scott Ray Laws is an unique and really cool songwriter…he digs into materials, tells a story in his songs, and has a clean baritone vocality that is easy on the ears. We had a chance to meet and hang with Scott back in May ..and I HAD to have him back for a Wednesday evening.” Luigi- Owner-The Listening Room.

“..An ORIGINAL songwriter who knows how to tell a story clearly in song” -  Scotty O’Neill - Guitarist/Promoter

“ It was such a treat catching your set last night — really refreshing to hear something new and original. Thanks for pulling up a chair and hanging out with us — we really enjoyed the conversation and the stories behind your songs.”  -Tripp B. - Sonoma Songwriter

“Expect slow burning passion and vivid music …the kind of energy that turns into “let’s stay for just one more!..”  - Doug- Owner/Wine Maker- Spicy Vines

“...His lyrics simply tell first-person stories from his own life. Nothing fancy, he's not writing to impress--he pours himself, as is, into each phrase and melody.”- Rebecca Roudman- Dirty Cello Radio Hour KRCB Radio 104.9 FM

“ It is through forthright lyrics that are personal and earnest, that he composes lyrical pictures. Taking snapshots from the most common walks of life...”  - David Sampson - Producer Studio Secti West

“..relaxed mid-tempo Americana, capturing in each song the rhythmic pocket Laws is known for creating.” -  Coyote Music Review 2024

title: Bottega Cellar Series with Stony Hill Vineyard & Heitz Cellar
description:
Join us at Bottega on December 2nd for an elegant evening featuring Stony Hill Vineyard and Heitz Cellar, hosted by Carlton McCoy Jr., Master Sommelier and CEO of Lawrence Wine Estates. Lawrence Wine Estates' Stony Hill Vineyard and Heitz Cellar are two of Napa Valley's most storied wineries. Founded on Spring Mountain in 1952 by the McCrea family, Stony Hill built its legacy on high-elevation Chardonnay and Riesling, becoming known as one of America's great white wine producers. Heitz Cellar, founded in 1961 by Joe and Alice Heitz, pioneered single-vineyard designated wines with Napa's first vineyard-designated Cabernet Sauvignon, helping establish the very idea of site-specific terroir in the valley. Hosted by the dynamic Carlton McCoy, Master Sommelier and CEO of Lawrence Wine Estates. Guests will experience a thoughtfully curated progression of wines highlighting two of Napa Valley’s most distinctive wineries, moving from expressive Chardonnay to a remarkable selection of Cabernet Sauvignon from Spring Mountain, Rutherford, and Oakville. The wines will be paired with a seasonal multi-course menu by Bottega Executive Chef Alex Espinoza, with each course designed to complement their character and expression while showcasing refined flavors, exceptional ingredients, and the gracious hospitality that defines Bottega.

Price is inclusive of tax and gratuity.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

 The three jurors, Ferdinanda Florence, Nadja Fitchhorn, and Vickie Marchand have spoken and made their selections!

We received 200 art entries from 67 talented artists representing 15 different cities throughout Northern California, making this an exciting and impressive year for our Juried Art Show.

It was wonderful to see so many artists arrive with their treasured works of art, eager to have them reviewed and considered by our three distinguished jurors.

After careful deliberation, the jurors selected 97 outstanding works of art to be included in this year's Juried Art Show!

title: Hispanic Chamber Young Professionals (HCYP) Monthly Networking Fiesta
Reimagining the Rain in Corona/Capri Creek
description:
*Si hablas español, habrá un intérprete en este evento. Indícanoslo en el último paso al inscribirte en el evento.*

***What would it look like if our neighborhoods were designed to work with and welcome water instead of sending it away?***

As a part of our **Harvest the Rain Pilot Program**, Daily Acts is inviting Petaluma community members who live near or are frequent visitors in the **Corona/Capri Creek** area to **REIMAGINE THE RAIN** by attending an interactive, neighborhood-based community input session.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**Join this Community Input Session to:**

*\-Help us understand your experience with stormwater*

*\-Learn from local experts in our community*

*\-Connect with your neighbors over* ***FREE dinner***

*\-Provide feedback on DIY rain garden and curb cut templates*

*\-Enter a* ***gift card drawing*** *for local businesses like Petaluma Coffee & Tea, Refill Mercantile and The Seed Bank!*

During the session, we'll discuss **how we can** **work with rainwater** to build resilient neighborhoods. We’ll hear from you to learn where you’ve noticed water pooling in your neighborhood, and explore whether those places are creating challenges, or if they could be the beginning of an opportunity to work with water in an exciting new way! We will also gather your feedback on the rain garden and curb-cut landscape templates we’re developing.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

***lf you live near or frequent Corona/Capri Creek, we want to hear from you!***

Come share your observations, what you’d like to see in your neighborhood, and any questions, excitement or concerns you may have about this pilot program. We hope to see you there!

*Questions? Please email* ***moreinfo@dailyacts.org*** *or call* ***(707) 200-8364***

This is an exciting opportunity to explore ways to create a safer, more welcoming, accessible, and vibrant neighborhood park for everyone to enjoy.

What Would You Like to See at Wilson Park? Your ideas can help identify potential park improvements, including:

New recreational amenities and play features

Safer, more accessible spaces for all ages and abilities

Landscaping, shade, and beautification

Family-friendly gathering and relaxation areas

Opportunities for recreation, wellness, and neighborhood connections

No final renovation plan has been selected. Community input will help guide the proposed improvements.

title: Bachata Beginners Thursday
description:
Your First Steps into Bachata

This class is perfect for bachata beginners that want to learn basic steps and skills, or those who want to refresh their foundational skills. We understand that learning something new can feel a little intimidating. That’s why our supportive and relaxed environment is specifically designed to make learning bachata basics an absolute blast!

Our friendly instructors will guide you through:

**Basic directional steps:** You’ll learn the fundamental movements that form the building blocks of all bachata dancing.

**Proper frame for partner work:** Discover how to connect comfortably and effectively with a partner, setting you up for smooth and enjoyable dances.

**Simple turn patterns:** We’ll introduce you to easy-to-follow turn patterns that will have you dancing with a partner in no time.

We’ve carefully organized our curriculum to ensure that each movement is easy to grasp and remember, building your confidence with every step. Our goal is to make learning fun. Join us to learn Bachata in Marin.

Important Details

**No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

Please wear **non-marking shoe soles:** This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

Come join us and discover the joy of bachata! We can’t wait to see you on the dance floor.

title: Samba no Pé
description:
Get ready to feel the rhythm and energy of Rio de Janeiro! **Samba no Pé** (Samba in the Foot) is the captivating solo style of samba danced in the streets and at Carnival, known for its rapid, intricate footwork and infectious hip movements.

**You will learn**

The Basic Step: You will master the signature quick-quick-slow rhythm that defines Samba no Pé.

Arm & Hip Styling: You will learn how to add the authentic flair, movement, and energy that makes Brazilian samba so captivating.

Technique & Posture: You will receive tips on proper body alignment to help you dance longer, faster, and more safely.

Rhythm & Musicality: You will learn how to connect your movement directly to the irresistible beat of the bateria (the samba drum section).

This class is perfect for anyone looking to connect with the vibrant spirit of Brazil, improve coordination, and get a fantastic workout—all while learning the foundational steps of this iconic dance. No partner or prior dance experience is required! Just bring your enthusiasm and comfortable shoes!

Date & Time: Thursdays @6:30PM – 7:30PM

Address: 4140 Redwood Highway #8 San Rafael, CA

Note: Arrive 10 minutes before. No floor marking shoe soles allowed.

description:
She knows exactly the kind of guy she wants, but grandmother Bubbe and the matchmaker think differently. 

This nostalgic favorite was made into a beloved film in 1988. It is a love story about Izzy, a thoroughly modern woman with not the greatest taste in men. Her grandmother Bubbe is desperate to get her married. Enter Henka, the matchmaker with a New York accent so sharp it could cut cheese, and Sam Posner, the pickle man with the heart of a poet. Will Izzy make the right choice? Doors open half an hour early for a photographic slideshow about New York’s Lower East Side, and some special snacks: Babka and Brooklyn Egg Creams. Don’t miss this delightful romantic comedy suitable for ages 8 and up. 

Playwright: Susan Sandler

Director: Amanda Claiborne

Starring: Kathy Ping-Rogers, Kimy Martinez-Knight, Nick Stewart, Karen Clancy and Jake Hamlin

**Trigger warnings:** Mention of suicide and some mild cursing in Yiddish. Suitable for ages 8 and up.

title: Gain Speaking Confidence with Mare Island Toastmasters
description:
We meet in-person only on the 1st and 2nd Thursdays of the month. However, you can catch us online every Thursday unless the meeting date falls on a holiday.

Please register at https://signup.com/go/WiniixA

What is Toastmasters About?

Usually at our meetings, we will have a prepared speech, and a speech evaluation. The Grammarian and Wizard of Ah's will listen for turns of phrases and the use of filler words. We also practice impromptu speaking during the section of the meeting called Table Topics. During Table Topics, at a recent meeting, we were asked what we felt was the biggest communication problem or challenge. What would you answer in a fast moment? Table topics will challenge you to think quickly and give an answer without preparation.

You will also hear tips on public speaking skills at our upcoming meeting. Whether you're a seasoned traveler or just looking for some adventure from the comfort of your home, this event is perfect for you.

Toastmasters International is all about communication excellence, and for 100 years and counting, Toastmasters have been expressing themselves better, practicing, and evaluating in a fun club environment, shining all around the world.

title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Latkes, Light & Luncheon: A Cooking Class at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
description:
Join us for a seasonal cooking experience celebrating the Festival of Lights that brings together the best of holiday tradition and winter warmth.

In this immersive lunch-and-learn, Stephanie Klassen Rosenbaum will teach you step-by-step how to achieve the perfect crispy, golden potato latke paired with homemade applesauce. She will also share her secrets for crafting a deeply flavorful beet borscht and demonstrate how to elevate simple autumn side dishes—like roasted squash—with our very own award-winning balsamic vinegar.

After learning the techniques, you’ll gather at a cozy communal table to feast on all the dishes prepared. We'll finish the afternoon on a sweet note with a slice of warm, flaky pie crafted by Red Bird Bakery, featuring Gold Ridge Organic Farms heirloom apples.

What to Expect: A scenic ride in our apple-themed trolley from the Farm Shop to the Apple Cottage • A step-by-step cooking demonstration inside our Apple Cottage kitchen \(no cooking required on your part!\) • Expert tips and kitchen secrets from Stephanie Klassen Rosenbaum on crafting traditional dishes using fresh, local produce • A multi-course sit-down lunch featuring the day's harvest menu, enjoyed at a communal table in our organic orchard • Seasonal refreshments, including your choice of a vibrant citrus shrub or our freshly pressed apple cider • 10% off all Farm Shop purchases on the day of your class

Stephanie Klassen Rosenbaum is the author of seven cookbooks, including A Little Taste of San Francisco and Honey from Flower to Table. She has taught seasonal cooking at farmers markets and other venues from Brooklyn to Berkeley, including the Ferry Plaza Farmers' Market in San Francisco and the Gravenstein Apple Fair in Sebastopol. She has cooked at numerous artists' and writers' retreats including the Headlands Center for the Arts in Sausalito, and studied organic farming at the Center for Agrocology at UC Santa Cruz.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

Research has identified cognitive, physiological, and emotional benefits including: Stress Reduction and Relaxation Enhanced Cognitive Engagement Emotional Depth and Empathy Improved Observational Skills Mindfulness Psychological support Increased Perceived Beauty Social Connectedness No special knowledge of art or artists required, just a sense of curiosity. Some people find it useful to bring a journal or sketchbook as part of their looking tools. Some basic art materials will be available.

description:
Shut Up & Write!® Wine Country
**This event is hosted on the Shut Up & Write website, so please [sign up here](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2me5JeN600/id2w10OBEA00) for your writing event.**

**ABOUT THE EVENT**
Join us virtually for an hour + of writing using Zoom. Let's keep together as much as we can during these uncertain times and keep on writing. Look for the schedule online and join us.

We’ve discovered that it’s strikingly helpful to write with other writers. See if it’s true for you at 3pm on Friday afternoon. Be it a book, blog, script, essay, dissertation, resume, melody, poem or just plain work stuff, you are invited to write it with us. No one will see what you've written or give you unsolicited advice. Instead of just thinking about writing, come and get some real writing done.

JOIN US!

1. Link available on the Shut Up and Write website..

Please note:

1. If you don't have Zoom set up on your computer yet, leave 15-30 minutes ahead of time to get it set up!
2. If you have difficulty with audio (don't have a microphone set up), as long as you have a speaker, you can call in (you'll see phone numbers when you log in).
3. If you are late, you won't be able to intro with us, but you are still welcome to join in.
4. If you won't be able to make it, please cancel so that the space is available to another writer.

SCHEDULE:
3:00 - quick intros.
around 3:10 - timer starts: write for 70 mins.
4:20 - (the end) wrap up

Wherever you are, we hope to see you online! Keep on writing...
Regards,
Lorraine Segal

title: Mare Island Light Night - Holiday Tree Celebration
description:
Light Night at Mare Island Friday, December 4 | 5-7pm | Historic Core

As dusk settles over the Strait, Mare Island glows. Come gather with neighbors for our annual Holiday Tree Lighting Celebration, a night of music, sweet treats, and community spirit.

Sip complimentary hot chocolate, nibble on cookies, and join us as we light the tree. Then enjoy a special performance by the VOENA Children’s Choir, whose beautiful voices will carry the celebration into the evening.

Warm up, give back. Bring a new or gently used coat, or a sleeping bag, to donate to Vallejo Together. Guests 21 and older who donate a coat will receive a complimentary seasonal cocktail or mocktail, compliments of The Mare Island Company.

About Vallejo Together

Vallejo Together was established as a community organization in 2010 by Founder Maria Guevara to rally community supporters and volunteers to meet the needs of Vallejo. In 2019, Vallejo Together became a fully recognized 501\(c\)3 non-profit organization and refined their mission and vision to focus on serving the unhoused population in Vallejo. Vallejo Together seeks to fulfill their mission of establishing reliable systems of care through collaborative partnerships, advocacy for sustainable solutions, and offering traveling resource center services to people without homes in Vallejo. To become a volunteer or for more information about Vallejo Together programs, services, and events, please visit www.VallejoTogether.org

About VOENA

VOENA's mission is "Uniting the World with Children's Voices." Representing more than 35 cultures, VOENA's young singers share a message of unity, peace, and connection through music. Their voices have been heard on some of the world's most celebrated stages, including the White House, Carnegie Hall, the London Olympic Games, and the World Expo in Japan.

title: Matt Jaffe
description: Matt Jaffe is an indie rock & roll singer/songwriter from San Francisco. Cutting his teeth on countless open mics around the Bay, Matt started taking music \(a little bit\) more seriously when Jerry Harrison of Talking Heads offered to produce his first record. Since then, Matt has continued to churn out more songs than he can remember the words to, perform on stages throughout the land \(opening and/or touring with the likes of Mavis Staples, Wilco, Bob Weir, Jackie Greene, Chuck Prophet, Melissa Etheridge, and Blues Traveler\), and collaborate with Tom Higgenson of the Plain White T's. Inspired by the likes of Elvis Costello, Tom Petty and Stephin Merritt, Matt is continuously writing and recording to build a songbook that honors his heroes.  Along with serving on Bread & Roses Board of Directors, he is currently rolling out his 7th studio album, Gone Enough to Miss.

Sonoma, CA— November 27 - Dec 27 – This 2026 winter season, New Moon Circus invites audiences to ‘La Lune Brille’ — memorable family fun and stunning artistry under the intimate and charming atmosphere of the ‘petite’ big top.

Meet the Winter moon and her frenemy, the Sun.  When the moon is pushed from the sky, she must find a way home to the stars. Come along the journey as she encounters mysterious beings and friendly creatures on the way.

A child pleasing origin myth told through impressive aerialists, jugglers, acrobats, and clever comedy, this show blends classic storybook atmosphere with celestial magic. La Lune Brille will surprise, dazzle and delight all ages.

description:
**Date:** Friday, December 4, 2026

**Time:** Doors 6 PM | Show 7 PM

**Tickets:** $10 Adv | $15 Door | Free for Coyote Sonoma Club Members

**Food Vendor:** Smoked & Baked Pizza

**Location:** Coyote Sonoma - 44F Mill Street, Healdsburg CA, 95448

**Ann Halen** is a Van Halen tribute band hailing from Novato, California—lead by singer extraordinaire Annie Scherer—dedicated to performing song-for-song album recreations with note-for note accuracy. The band focuses exclusively on the David Lee Roth era Van Halen tunes, and has been performing to rave reviews ever since their inception. With an awesome female lead singer and a roster of accomplished, virtuosic musicians, they are an amazing tribute to one of the greatest bands in rock-and-roll history.

**Bad Reputation** pays tribute to Joan Jett and the Blackhearts with precision and love—all the songs that you want to hear, plus some that you need to hear. 

The musicians behind Bad Reputation have decades of experience, as well as youthful exuberance.

As Joan Jett, RJ Rocket (aka Robin Pfefer) has been a NorCal fixture since the 80s. She's performed with Wild Brides, Yo! Pizzaface, No Use For A Name, Dr. Obvious, Cheap Date 13, and more. She's produced records for Cheap Date 13, Grit & Pluck, Buzzard, Megan McElroy, and others. She brings a true Rock and Roll heart to Bad Reputation.

Guitarist Connor Skünck Jr.- owner of the coolest guitar in the world, as well as more hair than the rest of the band combined. Definitely punches above his weight class.

Bassist Kevin “Popeye” Dee - Played trumpet at Katy Perry's sweet 16 birthday, then a chance encounter with Tom Waits convinced him in a roundabout way to play electric bass.

Drummer Nicky Thunders -Lives large, plays big, plus red beard. What's not to love?

Her grandmother Bubbe is desperate to get her married. Enter Henka, the matchmaker with a New York accent so sharp it could cut cheese, and Sam Posner, the pickle man with the heart of a poet. title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. Set in 1904 on the eve of the St. Louis World’s Fair, the story follows the Smith family through a year of romance, humor, and unexpected change. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. LOUIS is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Tams-Witmark LLC. concordtheatricals.com

This holiday season, Spreckels Theatre Company offers a heartwarming alternative to traditional seasonal fare with *Rooted*, a story about the messy, fierce love that keeps us grounded. An intelligent, gentle comedy by Deborah Zoe Laufer, *Rooted* plays Nov. 27 – Dec.13!

Emery is perfectly content living in her beloved treehouse, completely isolated from the world, communing with her plants. Meanwhile, down on the ground, her sister Hazel is thoroughly miserable, slaving away at a dead-end diner job just to survive and financially support Emery’s eccentric lifestyle. Looking on from the sidelines, Luanne is yearning for something, anything to bring true meaning into her life.

﻿The sisters' fragile ecosystem is completely upended when Emery’s YouTube videos documenting her plant experiments unexpectedly go viral. Almost overnight, her digital musings accidentally incite a full-blown CULT(!). As throngs of devoted truth-seekers congregate below the treehouse, the lives of all three women are plunged into chaos, compelling each woman to choose their own path and find their bliss.

title: Monica Da Silva & Complicated Animals
description:
Monica da Silva grew up living between The United States and Belém, Brazil, a city on the Amazon River. A love of travel and foreign language helped to forge her unique sound. 

 

Paralleling her life, da Silva's music contains an eclectic mix of Brazilian and American influences. Her sound can be classified as International Fusion, as it is heavily influenced by Brazilian music, namely Bossa Nova, but also incorporates elements of Lounge, Electronica, Indie Pop, and Worldbeat. Da Silva brings her cultural diversity to her songs, smoothly flowing between English, Portuguese, and Spanish.

 

In 2010, da Silva released her album "Brasilissima" . The record featured songs in both of her native languages - English and Portuguese. The first single "Aí Então", “was chosen by Putumayo World Music to be included on their compilation “Brazilian Beat”. The upbeat, psychedelic track "That's Not The Way" was chosen by the music director of ESPN to be played during the programming of The FIFA World Cup in 2014, alongside major recording artists Coldplay, Sérgio Mendes, Pitbull, Jennifer Lopez, The Black Eyed Peas, Stan Getz, and Astrud Gilberto. 

Da Silva's single "Soldado de Amor" \(2017\) has been featured in the BBC One series "The Replacement”, in the Paramount Network series "American Woman", and in a 2019 campaign for the designer Tory Burch.

Her music has also been featured in the series "Heartland", and in an ad for Patron Tequila. She is currently recording a new, full-length solo album, as well as writing and recording with her project, Complicated Animals.

Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: Laguna Stewards Day/ Dia de Laguna Stewards at Colgan Creek
description:
Join the Laguna de Santa Rosa Foundation and City of Santa Rosa at Lower Colgan Creek for a hands-on stewardship day! Help create Santa Rosa’s first Monarch Meadows by planting milkweed and native wildflowers to support monarch butterflies, bees, and other pollinators. Connect with nature, meet your neighbors, and help create a lasting habitat for local wildlife! We suggest wearing layers as it may be cold in the morning, long pants, closed-toe shoes, and sun protection. Bring a backpack, and a water bottle; we’ll bring the tools, gloves, extra water, and snacks. Only heavy rain cancels. All ages are welcome!

Big thank you to our Phase 3 project funders, which include the Department of Water Resources Urban Streams Restoration Program, the Wildlife Conservation Board, and the Sonoma County Agricultural Preservation and Open Space District. Additional Phase 3 partners include the City of Santa Rosa and Rainforest Rising. Thank you Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation for the habitat kits. We could not do this work without them.

¡Únete a la Fundación Laguna de Santa Rosa y a la Ciudad de Santa Rosa en Lower Colgan Creek para un día de voluntariado y conservación! Ayúdanos a crear los primeros Prados de Mariposas Monarca de Santa Rosa, plantando algodoncillo y flores silvestres nativas para apoyar a las mariposas monarca, las abejas y otros polinizadores. ¡Conéctate con la naturaleza, conoce a tus vecinos y contribuye a crear un hábitat duradero para la fauna local! Sugerimos usar pantalones largos, zapatos cerrados y protección solar. Se recomienda traer una mochila y una botella de agua; nosotros llevaremos las herramientas, los guantes, agua extra y refrigerios. Solo se cancela por lluvia intensa. ¡Son bienvenidas personas de todas las edades!

Agradecemos enormemente a los financiadores de la Fase 3 del proyecto, entre ellos el Programa de Restauración de Arroyos Urbanos del Departamento de Recursos Hídricos, la Junta de Conservación de la Vida Silvestre y el Distrito de Preservación Agrícola y Espacios Abiertos del Condado de Sonoma. Otros socios de la Fase 3 incluyen la Ciudad de Santa Rosa y Rainforest Rising. Gracias a Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation por los kits de hábitat. ¡Sin ellos, no podríamos realizar este trabajo!

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan. 

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: You are Invited to North Bay Speech Masters Toastmasters Club Meeting
description:
Whether it's improving our health, focusing on professional advancement, learning a new skill, it is often helpful to obtain someone to help learn new skills like speaking without preparation. The group at Toastmasters can help.

We call speaking without preparation, impromptu speaking. If you want to learn new Impromptu speaking skills, Toastmasters can help. During the meeting, we will practice our impromptu speaking skills during our session we call Table Topics. During the Table Topics, the speaker is given a question, and they are asked to speak for 60 seconds to 2 minutes about the question.

Outside Toastmasters, impromptu speaking happens constantly. You might recognize it in moments such as:

--Being asked for your opinion in a meeting

--Responding to a follow-up question during a presentation

--Introducing yourself or someone else unexpectedly

--Handling a difficult or unplanned question

You can learn tips and tricks about speaking off the cuff at our meeting. Won't you join us and learn

what Toastmasters can do to help you on your professional journey.

Feel free to contact us for the zoon link at our website under the "Contact Us" button. The website is https://3038.toastmastersclubs.org

We hold meetings online and in-person. If joining us in-person, there is limited parking in the front lot. Once in the front door, please sign in at the computer to obtain a visitors' badge. \(IUsually, there is a sheet by the computer telling you how to log in for Toastmasters.\) If the sheet isn't there, the clerk at the desk can help. Then take the elevator down to the second floor, and take a left out of the elevator and a left at the hall and come down to the meeting room.

title: Holiday Cheeseboard Workshop at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
description:
Elevate your holiday entertaining and learn the ultimate skills to wow your guests this festive season!

Join Gold Ridge Organic Farms' resident cheese expert, Alli Keyser-Marti, for an intimate, hands-on cheeseboard workshop designed to help you create show-stopping displays for your holiday gatherings. Explore how to create your own beautiful board, showcasing a wide array of flavors, textures, and colors. Learn how to incorporate a variety of edible flowers and fresh herbs, local honey, apple cider syrup, balsamic vinegar, EVOO, olives, artisan bread, crackers, and dips to accompany the best local cheeses made by artisan producers from Sonoma County and beyond.

All ingredients and materials included in ticket price. You'll get to take home your creation to share with friends and family.

Building on a culinary career starting in her teenage years, in 2014 Alli Keyser-Marti fell in love with exploring the world of milk, salt, enzymes, and microbes. Her cheese journey includes managing Cowgirl Creamery’s original Pt Reyes shop, overseeing the Oliver’s Market Stony Point cheese department, as well as being awarded an ACEF Scholarship to attend the American Cheese Society's Portland conference in 2022, where she successfully completed the Certified Cheese Professional® exam. In 2025, Alli also became an ACS Certified Cheese Sensory Evaluator® and judged cheese for the Good Food Awards. She has followed this passion from her backyard in California to small farms all over France, rural Ohio, roadside stands in Sardinia, and ferries in Croatia. Most recently you’ll find her skillfully pairing cheese with olive oil and apple tastings at Gold Ridge Organic Farms, as well as overseeing our custom olive milling operations and maintaining our organic certifications.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Saturdays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? You’ve mastered the basics, now it’s time to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

**What You’ll Learn**

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

**• The Cross Body Lead (CBL) Series:** Master both **Inside and Outside Turns**, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

**• The “I Turn – You Turn”:** A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

**• The Walk-Through:** Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

**• Footwork & Shine:** We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

**Technique & Artistry**

Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

**• The Frame:** Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

**• Upper Body Mechanics:** Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

**• Connection:** Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

**Important Details**

**• No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

title: Weekend Santa Sightings
description:
Celebrate the holidays and join us at the Village for photos with Santa happening on weekends from Saturday, November 28th to Sunday, December 20th, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. daily.

Appointments are highly recommended, as we cannot guarantee that we can accommodate all walk-ups throughout the event series. Reserve your 5-minute window now for a $35 fee during our initial release (through Friday, November 13). Beginning Saturday, November 14, the fee increases to $45. Each family will receive a print to take home that day, as well as a digital copy of their photo following the appointment. Please note that we do not call or text waitlisted guests.\*

Make the most of your Santa visit:

Your photo package includes up to five digital photos, emailed the Monday following your appointment, plus a print to take home that day.

Enjoy writing letters to Santa and dropping them off at the official Montgomery Village Santa Mail mailbox, plus crafts at our holiday craft tables.

Sweeten your visit! Stop by Salt & Straw before or after your appointment and enjoy a complimentary kids’ scoop with any ice cream purchase during Weekend Santa Sightings (valid each Saturday and Sunday from 11/28/26 to 12/20/26 between 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.).

Keep an eye out for ME SPA’s elves, spreading holiday cheer and a little stress relief with special cards to redeem at the spa. Bring yours in for a Chill Bag, a holiday survival kit filled with goodies and coupons to help you keep your cool all season long. For an extra moment of relaxation, enjoy a complimentary chair massage as scheduling allows.

Retro Foto will be assisting in making this memory last a lifetime by providing Santa with a vintage ride for all to enjoy! Retro Foto is Sonoma County’s boutique photo booth experience. Lola is a fully restored 1970 Volkswagen bus that loves the camera – whether it’s as a photo booth or a photo backdrop! Lola is all about making memories, which is why Santa thought this would be the perfect way to drive into the Holiday season!

By attending this event, guests consent to appear in photo/video recordings that may be used for website photography or other purposes.

\*A portion of proceeds will benefit Sonoma County Secret Santa Program.

title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. Set in 1904 on the eve of the St. Louis World’s Fair, the story follows the Smith family through a year of romance, humor, and unexpected change. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. LOUIS is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Tams-Witmark LLC. concordtheatricals.com

Sonoma, CA— November 27 - Dec 27 – This 2026 winter season, New Moon Circus invites audiences to ‘La Lune Brille’ — memorable family fun and stunning artistry under the intimate and charming atmosphere of the ‘petite’ big top.

Meet the Winter moon and her frenemy, the Sun.  When the moon is pushed from the sky, she must find a way home to the stars. Come along the journey as she encounters mysterious beings and friendly creatures on the way.

A child pleasing origin myth told through impressive aerialists, jugglers, acrobats, and clever comedy, this show blends classic storybook atmosphere with celestial magic. La Lune Brille will surprise, dazzle and delight all ages.

description:

Her grandmother Bubbe is desperate to get her married. Enter Henka, the matchmaker with a New York accent so sharp it could cut cheese, and Sam Posner, the pickle man with the heart of a poet. Will Izzy make the right choice? Doors open half an hour early for a photographic slideshow about New York’s Lower East Side, and some special snacks: Babka and Brooklyn Egg Creams. Monica Da Silva & Complicated Animals
description:
Monica da Silva grew up living between The United States and Belém, Brazil, a city on the Amazon River. A love of travel and foreign language helped to forge her unique sound. 

 

Paralleling her life, da Silva's music contains an eclectic mix of Brazilian and American influences. Her sound can be classified as International Fusion, as it is heavily influenced by Brazilian music, namely Bossa Nova, but also incorporates elements of Lounge, Electronica, Indie Pop, and Worldbeat. Da Silva brings her cultural diversity to her songs, smoothly flowing between English, Portuguese, and Spanish.

 

In 2010, da Silva released her album "Brasilissima" . The record featured songs in both of her native languages - English and Portuguese. The first single "Aí Então", “was chosen by Putumayo World Music to be included on their compilation “Brazilian Beat”. The upbeat, psychedelic track "That's Not The Way" was chosen by the music director of ESPN to be played during the programming of The FIFA World Cup in 2014, alongside major recording artists Coldplay, Sérgio Mendes, Pitbull, Jennifer Lopez, The Black Eyed Peas, Stan Getz, and Astrud Gilberto. 

Da Silva's single "Soldado de Amor" \(2017\) has been featured in the BBC One series "The Replacement”, in the Paramount Network series "American Woman", and in a 2019 campaign for the designer Tory Burch.

Her music has also been featured in the series "Heartland", and in an ad for Patron Tequila. She is currently recording a new, full-length solo album, as well as writing and recording with her project, Complicated Animals.

Emery is perfectly content living in her beloved treehouse, completely isolated from the world, communing with her plants. Meanwhile, down on the ground, her sister Hazel is thoroughly miserable, slaving away at a dead-end diner job just to survive and financially support Emery’s eccentric lifestyle. Looking on from the sidelines, Luanne is yearning for something, anything to bring true meaning into her life.

﻿The sisters' fragile ecosystem is completely upended when Emery’s YouTube videos documenting her plant experiments unexpectedly go viral. Almost overnight, her digital musings accidentally incite a full-blown CULT(!). As throngs of devoted truth-seekers congregate below the treehouse, the lives of all three women are plunged into chaos, compelling each woman to choose their own path and find their bliss.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

We hold an in-person meetings at 9:30 on Sunday mornings at Church of the Nazarene, 18980 Arnold Drive, Sonoma, CA \(a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted\) and newcomers are always welcome.

You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does not endorse any specific food plan.

Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. title: Petaluma River Upstream High Tide Paddle
description:
When the tide is high, the Petaluma River opens into a quieter, greener world.

Join The Floathouse crew at their central downtown dock for a gentle, guided paddle upstream, timed to higher tides that allow access beyond the downtown channel and into a tranquil tidal slough. With extra water beneath us, we’re able to glide into calm, lush stretches of the river that are normally out of reach.

This unhurried paddle highlights the natural beauty of the Petaluma River’s brackish, tidal waterway. Watch for great egrets, blue herons, snowy egrets, turtles basking along the banks, and abundant plant life. The calm water and peaceful surroundings create a deeply grounding experience—many guests say they feel their stress melt away within minutes.

Along the way, knowledgeable guides share stories of the river’s ecology and human history, offering insight into how this upper channel has shaped—and continues to shape—Petaluma. It’s a rare opportunity to experience how close wild nature lives to the heart of downtown.

Beginner-friendly. Sit-on-top kayaks and all gear provided.
