For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: "Ninety Minute Live Painting" Demonstration & Book Signing
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Presenter: Craig Nelson

Date: Sunday, December 6th

Time: 2PM-4PM

Location: Santa Rosa Store

Free!






Join us for an inspiring and educational live painting demonstration with renowned artist Craig Nelson. During this demonstration, Craig will showcase oil painting techniques that allow him to create beautiful and dynamic paintings in 90 minutes.

After the demonstration, Craig will be available to answer questions and sign copies of his new book, Ninety Minute Live Paintings.

Ninety Minute Live Paintings collects 206 paintings made during live 90-minute virtual sessions, held weekly over four years starting in March 2020. What began as a way to bring joy to an uncertain time became a ritual Craig has continued ever since. The book is as much a document of that period as it is a collection of the work itself.

Craig Nelson began his career as an illustrator in 1970, working with clients like Toyota, the U.S. Air Force, and UCLA, and creating portraits and album covers for figures including Neil Simon, Sammy Davis Jr., and Natalie Cole. For the past 35 years, his focus has been Fine Art — rich, vibrant oils spanning portraits, landscapes, and urban scenes — earning 40+ solo exhibitions, 200+ awards, and national medals. He has taught at the university level since 1974 and currently serves as Executive Director of Fine Art Painting at Academy of Art University. His sought-after summer plein air workshops have taken students throughout Europe, with past adventures in Italy, Sicily, Holland, France, Austria, Amalfi, Ischia, and a new journey planned for August 2027 in Cotswolds and Cornwall.

RSVP to reserve your spot!

title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. Set in 1904 on the eve of the St. Louis World’s Fair, the story follows the Smith family through a year of romance, humor, and unexpected change. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. LOUIS is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Tams-Witmark LLC. concordtheatricals.com

description:
This holiday season, Spreckels Theatre Company offers a heartwarming alternative to traditional seasonal fare with *Rooted*, a story about the messy, fierce love that keeps us grounded. An intelligent, gentle comedy by Deborah Zoe Laufer, *Rooted* plays Nov. 27 – Dec.13!

Emery is perfectly content living in her beloved treehouse, completely isolated from the world, communing with her plants. Meanwhile, down on the ground, her sister Hazel is thoroughly miserable, slaving away at a dead-end diner job just to survive and financially support Emery’s eccentric lifestyle. Looking on from the sidelines, Luanne is yearning for something, anything to bring true meaning into her life.

﻿The sisters' fragile ecosystem is completely upended when Emery’s YouTube videos documenting her plant experiments unexpectedly go viral. Almost overnight, her digital musings accidentally incite a full-blown CULT(!). As throngs of devoted truth-seekers congregate below the treehouse, the lives of all three women are plunged into chaos, compelling each woman to choose their own path and find their bliss.

title: St Peter's Chapel Concert Series & VOENA present: Voices of Peace on Earth
description: "Peace on Earth... Goodwill to All." In a world longing for hope, there is one language that every heart understands. Hold your breath as the angelic voices of VOENA take the stage amidst the breathtaking beauty of original Tiffany stained glass windows. Dressed in elegant Victorian attire, VOENA's singers will fill the historic St. Peter's Chapel with harmonies that transcend borders, cultures, and generations. Experience the magic of the season in one of the most treasured landmarks on the West Coast-St. Peter's Chapel, the oldest Navy chapel on the West Coast and the second oldest in the United States, dating back to 1901. Surrounded by glowing light, timeless architecture, and the warmth of human connection, this extraordinary holiday celebration invites you to experience the true spirit of the season through song, story, and soul. Jjoining the celebration is acclaimed Taiko artist David Gonzalez, carrying on the tradition of Taiko Grandmaster Seiichi Tanaka, the father of Taiko in North America. Together, their powerful rhythms and VOENA's soaring voices create a universal heartbeat of connection and peace. At the heart of every VOENA performance is a profound mission: Uniting the World Through Children's Voices. Representing more than 35 cultures, VOENA has inspired audiences on some of the world's greatest stages-including the White House, Carnegie Hall, the London Olympic Games, the World Expo in Japan, and performances for the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi. Audiences are not simply spectators-they are immersed, uplifted, and transformed. Voices of Peace on Earth is more than a holiday concert; it is a celebration of hope, compassion, and the belief that music has the power to bring humanity together. Prepare to be surrounded by soaring voices, breathtaking percussion, radiant stained glass, and unforgettable moments of beauty as VOENA shares the season's greatest gift: Peace on Earth. Proud Mary is a new project brought to you by members of the San Francisco Bay Area's most popular tribute bands and original rock groups. Led by the soulful voice of lead singer, McKenzie Fulkerson-Jones \(they/them\), the group serves up a playful yet fierce take on CCR's music, with a side of rainbows, tassels and glitter. Joined by Linda Moody \(she/her\) on guitar, Tori Fulkerson-Jones \(she/her\) on bass and Jai Bird \(she/her\) on drums, Proud Mary will put a spell on you at their "Queerwater Revival."

Proud Mary delivers fresh performances of CCR's greatest hits and welcomes everyone to join in. Between the iconic guitar licks you expect and some surprising and interactive theatrical elements, you're sure to be on your feet, grooving and belting along to every song.

description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: Fortner-Clayton-Hamilton Trio
description: Together they create a trio steeped in swing, spontaneity, and deep musical conversation. Their performances celebrate the timeless language of the jazz trio while showcasing the individuality and brilliance of three extraordinary artists. The trio will draw in part froma program they performed together in Europe last summerthat celebrated the legacy of Oscar Peterson. In addition tomusic honoring Peterson's iconic trio tradition, the concert will also feature original compositions by each artist, showcasing the distinct voices of three of today's leading jazz musicians in an intimate and dynamic setting that bridges reverence for the past with the creative voices of today's leading improvisers. Sullivan Fortner won the Grammy Award for Best Jazz Instrumental Albumfor his album Southern Nights at the 68th Annual Grammy Awards on February 1, 2026. This marks his third career Grammy win. John Clayton, a Grammy Award-winning bassist, composer, and arranger, has performed and recorded with artists ranging from Diana Krall and Paul McCartney to Yo-Yo Ma. A former principal bassist of the Amsterdam Philharmonic Orchestra, he and Jeff Hamilton later co-founded the renowned Clayton-Hamilton Jazz Orchestra, one of the premier big bands in jazz today. Jeff Hamilton, a respected drummers in jazz, is known for his impeccable swing, taste, and musicality. Throughout his career he has performed with legends including Ray Brown, Oscar Peterson, and Monty Alexander, and remains a driving force behind the Clayton-Hamilton Jazz Orchestra as well as his own acclaimed trio.

title: St Peter's Chapel Candlelight Evening Concert "Voices of Peace on Earth"
description: "Peace on Earth... Goodwill to All." In a world longing for hope, there is one language that every heart understands. Enter an evening of candlelight, beauty, and connection as the angelic voices of VOENA fill the historic St. Peter's Chapel, surrounded by the breathtaking glow of original Tiffany stained glass windows. Dressed in elegant Victorian attire, VOENA's singers will illuminate the season with harmonies that transcend borders, cultures, and generations. As candlelight flickers throughout this treasured landmark-the oldest Navy chapel on the West Coast and the second oldest in the United States, dating back to 1901-you will be transported into a world of wonder, warmth, and timeless holiday spirit. Through song, story, and soul, this intimate celebration invites us to rediscover the true meaning of the season: compassion, unity, and peace. Also featured is acclaimed Taiko artist David Gonzalez, carrying on the tradition of Taiko Grandmaster Seiichi Tanaka, the father of Taiko in North America. Together, the thunderous heartbeat of Taiko and VOENA's soaring voices create a breathtaking celebration of connection and peace. At the heart of every VOENA performance is a profound mission: Uniting the World with Children's Voices. Representing more than 35 cultures, VOENA has inspired audiences on some of the world's greatest stages-including the White House, Carnegie Hall, the London Olympic Games, the World Expo in Japan, and performances for the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi. Audiences are not simply spectators-they are immersed, uplifted, and transformed. Voices of Peace on Earth is more than a holiday concert; it is a candlelit journey of hope, reminding us that music has the power to heal, inspire, and bring humanity together. Prepare to be surrounded by candlelight, soaring voices, breathtaking percussion, and unforgettable moments of beauty as VOENA shares the season's greatest gift: Peace on Earth. title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Mondays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: The Swingles: Together For The Holidays
description:
The Swingles have been challenging the boundaries of vocal music for over 60 years, earning 5 Grammy® Awards and establishing themselves as one of the world’s most beloved and admired vocal groups.

Throughout its various iterations \(Les Swingles Singers / Swingle II / The New Swingle Singers / The Swingles / The Swingle Singers \(and since 2014, The Swingles again\)\), the group's signature and instantly-recognisable sound has remained constant and timeless and their intricate arrangements remain unparalleled. The current singers are masters of their craft, constantly seeking new ways of reimagining jazz, folk, pop and classical music from their ever-growing repertoire, alongside creating a rich vein of new original material. Their combination of close-microphone amplification paired with the extraordinary range and vocal dexterity of the group’s seven individual voices to create one seamlessly-blended vocal sound, has captured the admiration of composers and collaborators alike, who have embraced the sheer versatility of the group and its genre-crossing possibilities.

American-born Ward Swingle first assembled a group of Parisian session singers to sing through Bach’s Well-Tempered Clavier as a vocal exercise in 1962. The resulting album ‘Jazz Sebastian Bach’ \(recorded initially for friends and family\), became a huge hit, breaking new musical ground and launching The Swingles to fame. Several of the singers had previously sung with Mimi Perrin’s group Les Double Six \(who with Quincy Jones and Dizzy Gillespie recorded the 6 voices twice in order to create a much larger sound and richer chord structure\). The Swingles of today employ a similar technique in their current shows - an immersive layering up of vocals using live-looping technology to record themselves in the moment and have it play back later, producing mesmeric \(and potentially massive\) musical textures.

The group has released more than 50 albums encompassing a huge range of music in many different styles, fuelled by Ward Swingle’s pioneering spirit and varied musical tastes. Their arrangements tend either to give a little twist to the original or turn it completely on its head. The group’s genre-inclusive approach to music-making has led to collaborations with artists such as Jamie Cullum, Gareth Malone, Kurt Elling, New York Voices, and Labrinth. They co-wrote and performed a song for the end credits of Alexander Payne’s film ‘Downsizing’ and have appeared on many film and TV soundtracks, including ‘Grey’s Anatomy’, ‘Sex and the City’, ‘Wedding Crashers’, ‘The Holdovers’, ‘The Two Popes’, and ‘Glee’.

"superhero singing to truly raise goosebumps.”

THE GUARDIAN

"The Swingles were never less than dazzling”

THE WASHINGTON POST

title: Poetic Medicine in Community: Healing Through Creativity and Connection: 12/8/2026 — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Poetic Medicine in Community: Healing Through Creativity and Connection: December 8th, 2026

  
    
      
        
          $15.00
        
      
    
  

Poetic Medicine in Community: Healing Through Creativity and ConnectionTuesday, December 8th, 4:00-5:30pm Class Description: Poetry can be a salve for the heart and soul. It is a way of speaking what is true in our hearts and is often difficult to access without a creative spark. You do not have to be a “poet” or even a “writer” to allow words and feeling to your through your pen. COME JOIN US!Writing poetry in community is a bit like attending a meditation retreat. The instruction for most beginners when learning to meditate is to simply bring oneself back to the breath, each time the mind wanders. In poem-making, the instruction is to bring oneself back to the heart and along with a deep breath, see if one can open a little bit wider. When we witness each other in this process, in a circle of open-heartedness, something magical happens!This is an IN-PERSON gathering in an open and safe creative community. We are all poets! Please bring your own writing materials. 22 students maximum. About the Instructor: Redwing Keyssar has been leading “Poetic Medicine in Community” sessions through her work in Palliative Care at UCSF since 2020. Her work has created an international community of people who, by listening to and writing poetry together, have healed wounds of grief and loss, helped ”wounded healers,” and provided resiliency to move forward on our life paths.Redwing is a Palliative Care nurse, educator and consultant, an end-of-life doula, author, poet, song-writer, ceremonialist, national presenter and frequent contributor to public issues about Palliative and End of Life Care. She is a Board member of the Sebastopol Senior Center and offers presentations about end-of-life issues throughout the Bay Area. Before working at the UCSF MERI CENTER, her professional career included being the Clinical Director at Zen Hospice Project and the Director of Palliative Care and Nursing at Jewish Family and Children’s Services from 2004-2018. She is a founder and adjunct faculty member of the California State University Shiley/Haynes Institute of Palliative Care and has taught courses at OLLI at Sonoma State. Redwing is the author of an award-winning book, “Last Acts of Kindness; Lessons for the Living from the Bedsides of the Dying” and is the recipient of numerous awards in the field of Palliative Care.She is passionate about utilizing poetry as a healing modality!

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Maple Magic & Winter Wonder
description:

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: Abstract Watercolor painting
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Join us for Abstract Watercolor Painting at Riley Street, Santa Rosa

Instructor: Anne Millett

Date: Tuesday, December 8th

Time: 11:00AM-2:30PM

Fee: $45.00


There will be over 70 high quality paint colors for you to choose from, plus 6 metallics. You will spend time selecting your colors intuitively, for the way they make you feel in the moment. This process is quite personal.

What we paint does not need to accurately represent real things that we see in the "outside world". We listen to our intuitions as our paintings build shape by shape, mark by mark, without planning the end result. We paint simply and methodically, focusing on putting paint on paper and seeing what happens, then where we'll go next.

High quality watercolor paint, very good brushes, 1 piece of Arches 140# cold press watercolor paper (and a second if you finish your first painting), and complete set-ups for painting in class will be provided.


This class is designed for adults 18+

All levels of experience welcome

title: Belly Dancing with Raja - Tuesdays
description:
DATE AND TIME: Tuesdays @ 11:00 AM

Unlock your inner strength and find your flow. Belly dancing with Raja is an innovative fusion class that blends the rhythmic artistry of belly dance with the high-energy benefits of aerobics. Designed to be both a cardiovascular challenge and a deep toning session, this class focuses on the “powerhouse” of the body—your core.

By layering fluid, isolative movements over an athletic aerobic base, you will challenge your muscles in ways traditional gym workouts can’t reach.

What to Expect in Belly Dancing Class

• Core-Centric Power: Use undulations and shimmies to engage deep abdominal muscles for a tighter, stronger midsection.

• Functional Stability: Improve your balance and posture through controlled, hip-driven movements and low-impact aerobic footwork.

• Total Body Toning: Build lean muscle in your legs, glutes, and arms while maintaining a constant, heart-pumping pace.

• Mind-Body Connection: Enhance your coordination and body awareness through rhythmic, expressive choreography.

“Whether you’re looking to define your waistline or simply want a workout that feels like a celebration, this class offers the perfect balance of sweat and grace.”

Difficulty Level: All levels welcome! No prior dance experience is required—just bring your energy and a willingness to move.

description:
*Si hablas español, habrá un intérprete en este evento. Indícanoslo en el último paso al inscribirte en el evento.*

***What would it look like if our neighborhoods were designed to work with and welcome water instead of sending it away?***

As a part of our **Harvest the Rain Pilot Program**, Daily Acts is inviting Petaluma community members who live near or are frequent visitors in the **Adobe Creek** area to **REIMAGINE THE RAIN** by attending an interactive, neighborhood-based community input session.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**Join this Community Input Session to:**

*\-Help us understand your experience with stormwater*

*\-Learn from local experts in our community*

*\-Connect with your neighbors over* ***FREE dinner***

*\-Provide feedback on DIY rain garden and curb cut templates*

*\-Enter a* ***gift card drawing*** *for local businesses like The Seed Bank, Caffeine Inc., and Refill Mercantile*

title: S.R. Laws
description:
S.R. LAWS IS OUT THERE: He approaches songwriting with a passion for songs that we all grew up on. His sound rings a familiar bell in your head while still delivering ideas completely unique.  He draws inspiration from outstanding storytellers like John Hiatt, Lucinda Williams, Rodney Crowell, Steve Earle, Neil Finn, Patty Griffin, Chuck Prophet, and Ron Sexsmith. All of their music and others have carved a deep groove. 

Growing up out there in Northern California, he developed a unique connection to music early on. His father worked as a trash collector, and he would spend hours sifting through bags of discarded 45 records. Each find felt like stumbling upon hidden treasures. Some records were covered in dirt and grime, while others were pristine. The thrill of discovering new sounds was exhilarating, and he could hardly wait to drop the needle and immerse himself in the music.

He embarked on a pilgrimage to Texas with just two suitcases and $500 in his bank account. His goal was to dive into the vibrant music scene and learn from fellow songwriters. Austin, known as the "Live Music Capital of the World," offered countless opportunities for him to grow as an artist. Open mics and songwriters' nights became his training ground, where he soaked up every moment, listening to others share their stories through music.

These days, he resides in Sonoma County, California, working hard as a touring artist and singer-songwriter for his original rock band, The Heartsleeves. He invites everyone to join him on this musical journey, sharing his songs one person at a time in this vast and unpredictable world we live in.

A.M. Sessions 

Check out the latest album from S.R. Laws-  "A.M. Sessions." It's a collection of songs that I am incredibly proud of, crafted with the help of old friends and intrepid new collaborators. I can tell you more about it sometime. Come out and grab a copy at one of the shows or you can find it online. “

“ It is through forthright lyrics that are personal and earnest, that he \(Laws\) composes lyrical pictures. Taking snapshots from the most common walks of life filtered through his own joy and tribulations.”  - David Sampson - Producer Studio Secti West

“..relaxed mid-tempo Americana, capturing in each song the rhythmic pocket Laws is known for creating.” -  Coyote Music Review 2024

“...His lyrics simply tell first-person stories from his own life. Nothing fancy, he's not writing to impress--he pours himself, as is, into each phrase and melody.”- Rebecca Roudman- Dirty Cello Radio Hour KRCB Radio 104.9 FM

“A.M. Sessions is worth your while.” - Wiley Koepp- Texas Drummer

title: Sound Bath with Laura Benson
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
Rest & Renew at our Sound Bath!
Support your nervous system, release anxiety and stress, and harmonize your body, mind and spirit on the 2nd Tuesday of every month! Laura Benson has a Masters in Intuition Medicine(R) and is a certified sound healer who will guide you through a gentle meditation before each sound bath session. Bring your own yoga mat & blanket and come ready to rest and renew! In the OCA Studio.
Sliding scale pricing $25-$35.
Register
A sound bath is a whole-body, immersive listening experience. During a sound bath, participants often sit or lie down, and are surrounded by the mostly non-melodic soundscapes created by a range of instruments played by the sound bath facilitator. Hence, they are “bathed” in sound.
Sound therapy is a non-invasive healing modality that utilizes the physical and physiological interactions of sound on our bodies and nervous systems to produce therapeutic results. In a sound healing session, specific sonic frequencies are used to soothe the central nervous system, calm the breath, and quiet the mind by encouraging the brain to move into more relaxed states, down from beta (fight-or-flight) and into theta and alpha waves. This increases present-moment awareness and reduces stress and anxiety. Sound baths have been found to be effective in improving mood, cognitive function, and overall mental, physical, and spiritual wellbeing.
Crystal bowl sound baths are particularly powerful in that each bowl is tuned to a specific frequency that corresponds with a different chakra, or energy center, of the body. Based on specific needs, a practitioner can focus on releasing tension or clearing out stuck energy in specific chakras by playing certain bowls or intervals.
While attending a sound bath, you may experience physical sensations brought out by the crystal sound bowls or gong, such as tingling in your limbs or scalp, slowing of your breathing, eye flutters, or small muscle spasms. Not to worry! These sensations often indicate the release of tension or emotional energy stored in the body’s energy systems.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: AI Mastery for LEADERS managing AI across the business
description: Using AI to Lead More Effectively Across the Business Artificial intelligence is changing how businesses operate, but for many leaders the challenge is not hearing about AI. The challenge is knowing what is actually useful, where to begin, and how to lead adoption without confusion or unnecessary risk. The Napa Chamber's AI Mastery for Leaders Workshop Series is designed for owners, executives, general managers, partners, and department leaders who want a practical way to guide AI adoption across the business. This is not another generic AI webinar or tool demo. It is an in-person, small-group workshop series built to help local business leaders understand where AI creates value, how to introduce it responsibly, and how to turn it into a practical advantage inside the organization. What you will learn and walk away with A practical framework for identifying where AI can create value in your business A governance framework for responsible AI use A clear view of which tasks should stay human-led and which can be AI-assisted A method for identifying and prioritizing high-impact AI opportunities across departments A better approach to organizing SOPs, documents, and internal knowledge for stronger AI output A practical process for piloting AI before rolling it out more broadly A draft roadmap for your next 6-12 months of AI adoption Who should attend Business owners Presidents and CEOs General managers Partners Practice administrators Senior department leaders

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Maple Magic & Winter Wonder
description:
As the days grow shorter and cooler, Sonoma Botanical Garden transforms with the beauty of the changing seasons. From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: FSVAA 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show
description:
2026 Juried Art Exhibit: Celebrating Northern California’s Artistic Excellence!

FSVAA proudly presents the 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show at the Solano Town Center Gallery – show opening is Friday, Nov 13. Gallery Hours are Wed thru Sun, 11am–6pm.

 The three jurors, Ferdinanda Florence, Nadja Fitchhorn, and Vickie Marchand have spoken and made their selections!

We received 200 art entries from 67 talented artists representing 15 different cities throughout Northern California, making this an exciting and impressive year for our Juried Art Show.

It was wonderful to see so many artists arrive with their treasured works of art, eager to have them reviewed and considered by our three distinguished jurors.

After careful deliberation, the jurors selected 97 outstanding works of art to be included in this year's Juried Art Show!

Congratulations to all the artists whose work was selected, and thank you to everyone who participated and helped make this year's show such a success.

EXHIBIT INFORMATION \(Save the Dates\):

• Art Show Reception /Awards Gala: Saturday, Dec 5, 2026, 3–5pm

• Reception /Poetry Reading: Saturday, Dec 19, 2026, 3–5pm

• Juror's Talk: Sunday, Jan 3, 2027, 1–3pm at the Solano Town Center Gallery  – Come hear our Jurors speak! Join us as they share their insights into the selection process, discuss what goes into choosing artwork for a juried exhibition, and offer a glimpse into their experience. As always, there will be time for a Q&A, so bring your questions!

5-6pm: Arrive, get settled, and kick things off with a short welcome sesh.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Maple Magic & Winter Wonder
description:
As the days grow shorter and cooler, Sonoma Botanical Garden transforms with the beauty of the changing seasons. From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: FSVAA 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show
description:
2026 Juried Art Exhibit: Celebrating Northern California’s Artistic Excellence!

FSVAA proudly presents the 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show at the Solano Town Center Gallery – show opening is Friday, Nov 13. Gallery Hours are Wed thru Sun, 11am–6pm.

 The three jurors, Ferdinanda Florence, Nadja Fitchhorn, and Vickie Marchand have spoken and made their selections!

We received 200 art entries from 67 talented artists representing 15 different cities throughout Northern California, making this an exciting and impressive year for our Juried Art Show.

It was wonderful to see so many artists arrive with their treasured works of art, eager to have them reviewed and considered by our three distinguished jurors.

After careful deliberation, the jurors selected 97 outstanding works of art to be included in this year's Juried Art Show!

Congratulations to all the artists whose work was selected, and thank you to everyone who participated and helped make this year's show such a success.

EXHIBIT INFORMATION \(Save the Dates\):

• Art Show Reception /Awards Gala: Saturday, Dec 5, 2026, 3–5pm

• Reception /Poetry Reading: Saturday, Dec 19, 2026, 3–5pm

• Juror's Talk: Sunday, Jan 3, 2027, 1–3pm at the Solano Town Center Gallery  – Come hear our Jurors speak! Join us as they share their insights into the selection process, discuss what goes into choosing artwork for a juried exhibition, and offer a glimpse into their experience. As always, there will be time for a Q&A, so bring your questions!

title: Lower Russian River Municipal Advisory Council Meeting December 10, 2026
Reimagining the Rain in Washington Creek
description:
*Si hablas español, habrá un intérprete en este evento. Indícanoslo en el último paso al inscribirte en el evento.*

***What would it look like if our neighborhoods were designed to work with and welcome water instead of sending it away?***

As a part of our **Harvest the Rain Pilot Program**, Daily Acts is inviting Petaluma community members who live near or are frequent visitors in the **Washington Creek** area to **REIMAGINE THE RAIN** by attending an interactive, neighborhood-based community input session.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**Join this Community Input Session to:**

*\-Help us understand your experience with stormwater*

*\-Learn from local experts in our community*

*\-Connect with your neighbors over* ***FREE dinner***

*\-Provide feedback on DIY rain garden and curb cut templates*

*\-Enter a* ***gift card drawing*** *for local businesses like Petaluma Coffee & Tea, Caffeine Inc., Refill Mercantile and The Seed Bank!*

During the session, we'll discuss **how we can** **work with rainwater** to build resilient neighborhoods. We’ll hear from you to learn where you’ve noticed water pooling in your neighborhood, and explore whether those places are creating challenges, or if they could be the beginning of an opportunity to work with water in an exciting new way! We will also gather your feedback on the rain garden and curb-cut landscape templates we’re developing. 

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

***lf you live near or frequent Washington Creek, we want to hear from you!***

Come share your observations, what you’d like to see in your neighborhood, and any questions, excitement or concerns you may have about this pilot program. We hope to see you there!

*Questions? Please email* ***moreinfo@dailyacts.org*** *or call* ***(707) 200-8364***

title: Bachata Beginners Thursday
description:
Your First Steps into Bachata

This class is perfect for bachata beginners that want to learn basic steps and skills, or those who want to refresh their foundational skills. We understand that learning something new can feel a little intimidating. That’s why our supportive and relaxed environment is specifically designed to make learning bachata basics an absolute blast!

Our friendly instructors will guide you through:

**Basic directional steps:** You’ll learn the fundamental movements that form the building blocks of all bachata dancing.

**Proper frame for partner work:** Discover how to connect comfortably and effectively with a partner, setting you up for smooth and enjoyable dances.

**Simple turn patterns:** We’ll introduce you to easy-to-follow turn patterns that will have you dancing with a partner in no time.

We’ve carefully organized our curriculum to ensure that each movement is easy to grasp and remember, building your confidence with every step. Our goal is to make learning fun. Join us to learn Bachata in Marin.

Important Details

**No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

Please wear **non-marking shoe soles:** This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

Come join us and discover the joy of bachata! We can’t wait to see you on the dance floor.

We meet in-person only on the 1st and 2nd Thursdays of the month. However, you can catch us online every Thursday unless the meeting date falls on a holiday.

Please register at https://signup.com/go/WiniixA

What is Toastmasters About?

Usually at our meetings, we will have a prepared speech, and a speech evaluation. The Grammarian and Wizard of Ah's will listen for turns of phrases and the use of filler words. We also practice impromptu speaking during the section of the meeting called Table Topics. During Table Topics, at a recent meeting, we were asked what we felt was the biggest communication problem or challenge. What would you answer in a fast moment? Table topics will challenge you to think quickly and give an answer without preparation.

You will also hear tips on public speaking skills at our upcoming meeting. Whether you're a seasoned traveler or just looking for some adventure from the comfort of your home, this event is perfect for you.

Toastmasters International is all about communication excellence, and for 100 years and counting, Toastmasters have been expressing themselves better, practicing, and evaluating in a fun club environment, shining all around the world.

title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. Set in 1904 on the eve of the St. Louis World’s Fair, the story follows the Smith family through a year of romance, humor, and unexpected change. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. LOUIS is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Tams-Witmark LLC. concordtheatricals.com

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Maple Magic & Winter Wonder
description:
As the days grow shorter and cooler, Sonoma Botanical Garden transforms with the beauty of the changing seasons. From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: FSVAA 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show
description:
2026 Juried Art Exhibit: Celebrating Northern California’s Artistic Excellence!

FSVAA proudly presents the 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show at the Solano Town Center Gallery – show opening is Friday, Nov 13. Gallery Hours are Wed thru Sun, 11am–6pm.

 The three jurors, Ferdinanda Florence, Nadja Fitchhorn, and Vickie Marchand have spoken and made their selections!

We received 200 art entries from 67 talented artists representing 15 different cities throughout Northern California, making this an exciting and impressive year for our Juried Art Show.

It was wonderful to see so many artists arrive with their treasured works of art, eager to have them reviewed and considered by our three distinguished jurors.

After careful deliberation, the jurors selected 97 outstanding works of art to be included in this year's Juried Art Show!

Congratulations to all the artists whose work was selected, and thank you to everyone who participated and helped make this year's show such a success.

EXHIBIT INFORMATION \(Save the Dates\):

• Art Show Reception /Awards Gala: Saturday, Dec 5, 2026, 3–5pm

• Reception /Poetry Reading: Saturday, Dec 19, 2026, 3–5pm

• Juror's Talk: Sunday, Jan 3, 2027, 1–3pm at the Solano Town Center Gallery  – Come hear our Jurors speak! Join us as they share their insights into the selection process, discuss what goes into choosing artwork for a juried exhibition, and offer a glimpse into their experience. As always, there will be time for a Q&A, so bring your questions!

title: Nov & Dec Artwalks: "Moments in the Light"  Plein Air Painting
description:
Plein Air painting is painting on location responding to the environment as it moves you. For us it’s not about the details or exact characteristics of a location but rather the interaction of color, the atmosphere, the feeling of standing out there. It's about the immediate moment of seeing which is in the brushwork of several of the artists, creating a dialogue with the space as you make the marks and see how they correspond to what's in front of you. There is no right or wrong because it is a very personal moment. It's not impressionism. It's not quite expressionism. But it's the immediacy of being alive. 

Most of the paintings were done when Barry convinced one of the other artists to come painting with him. Creating a synergy from the overlapping influence on each other while keeping a distinct POV.

title: Winter Wonder Lantern Walks
description:
Celebrate the beauty and quiet magic of the season during Winter Wonder Lantern Walks, a festive after-dark experience at Sonoma Botanical Garden. Guided along the route by Garden staff and volunteers, guests will stroll through the winter landscape carrying glowing lanterns, discovering softly shadowed pathways, towering trees, and the peaceful stillness of the Garden beneath the night sky. Rather than a traditional docent-led tour, this experience is designed as a peaceful and immersive opportunity to enjoy the rare experience of walking through the Garden after hours and after dark. Along the way, enjoy moments of reflection, seasonal ambiance, and the simple joy of gathering outdoors during the holiday season.

The evening begins with hot cocoa, spiced cider, wine tasting and cookies from 5:30–6:00 p.m., followed by a brief welcome and lantern walk orientation before departing together for a guided walk through the Garden.

Winter Wonder Lantern Walks are a seasonal fundraiser that will support the Garden’s programs, collections, and conservation efforts. PLEASE READ the important accessibility and experience information, along with the registration and cancellation policy below before purchasing tickets.

title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. Set in 1904 on the eve of the St. Louis World’s Fair, the story follows the Smith family through a year of romance, humor, and unexpected change. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. This holiday season, Spreckels Theatre Company offers a heartwarming alternative to traditional seasonal fare with *Rooted*, a story about the messy, fierce love that keeps us grounded. An intelligent, gentle comedy by Deborah Zoe Laufer, *Rooted* plays Nov. 27 – Dec.13!

Emery is perfectly content living in her beloved treehouse, completely isolated from the world, communing with her plants. Meanwhile, down on the ground, her sister Hazel is thoroughly miserable, slaving away at a dead-end diner job just to survive and financially support Emery’s eccentric lifestyle. As throngs of devoted truth-seekers congregate below the treehouse, the lives of all three women are plunged into chaos, compelling each woman to choose their own path and find their bliss.

title: David Luning
description:
John Prine forced David Luning to drop out of college. Not at gunpoint or anything—the two had never even met—but the effect of hearing the songwriting legend's music for the first time had an equally compelling effect on Luning, who was studying film scoring at the Berklee College of Music in Boston at the time. Now an accomplished artist in his own right, Luning is preparing to release his most dynamic and gripping collection to date, 'Restless,' and he can trace it all back to one fateful night that changed everything.

"A couple of friends invited me over to share some songs at their apartment, and that was the first time I'd ever really listened to Americana music or folk or country or whatever you want to call it," remembers Luning. "They showed me John Prine, and it just resonated with me so much. I was like, 'Oh my god, this is what I have to do with my life.' I just figured it out in that moment."

Luning dropped out of school almost immediately, moved back to his native California, and devoted himself to songwriting and performing. He worked his way up through open mics to large festival performances, piecing together a band to flesh out his songs along the way and hitting the road to tour with a fierce determination. His self-released debut album, 'Just Drop On By,' garnered acclaim from both critics and fellow musicians alike, with country megastar Keith Urban hailing Luning's "staunch originality." Songs from the album landed numerous film and TV placements, most recently on NBC's 'Grimm,' and Luning's reputation for exhilarating live performances earned him dates with luminaries like Jackie Greene, Dave and Phil Alvin, and Elvin Bishop, along with a slew of festival performances up and down the West Coast.

If 'Just Drop On by' announced the arrival of a promising new talent, 'Restless' delivers on that potential and then some. Recorded under the guidance of engineer/producer Karl Derfler \(Tom Waits, Dave Matthews\) and with Luning's longtime live bandmates—Ben Dubin \(bass & harmonica\), Linden Reed \(drums\), and Dave Sampson \(guitar & mandolin\)—the album marks a major step forward, both sonically and emotionally.

"With the first record, I produced and engineered everything myself," explains Luning. "I'd never worked with an outside producer before, so it was nerve-racking going into the studio with Karl for the first time, but it was just a perfect fit. It was like he knew what I wanted in my music before I even did, and he could push my performances where they needed to go and really take my music to another level."

Luning and his band set up shop at the stunning Panoramic Studios in Stinson, California, crafting a darker, grittier vibe for the music and exploring a wider palette than ever before. While many of Luning's songs are inspired by the lives and stories of the men and women he's grown up with in California or met on the road, the lyrics are all filtered through his own unique perspective and reflect his remarkable personal journey. Perhaps no track fits that bill more directly than "Driftin,'" an infectious road warrior's anthem that find's Luning singing, "I wanna keep on drifting like a rambling man."

"I had so much fun on tour going from place to place and playing to new people all the time and I got into the rhythm of it all, so when it ended and we came home I wasn't ready to stop," he explains. "We pulled into Ben's house to unload our gear and I said, 'Ben, we're packing up and we're gonna go somewhere tomorrow right? We're gonna keep on going right?'"

Much of the album is uptempo and exuberant—"Almost Sounds Like Laughing" is a foot-stomping folk tune with the energy of a runaway train—but Luning shows off his remarkable depth and range on some of the record's more restrained tracks, like the slow-burning "Brother In Chains" and delicate "Gonna Forget About You," which finds him pulling his vocals back to an intimate near-whisper that conveys a world of heartache and regret. "In Hell I Am" started life as an acoustic blues on a resonator guitar before morphing into a fiery, electric rocker, while "Bet It All On Black" takes on a harder, Southern edge, with Luning repeating the mantra, "Ain't no use in holding back."

"It's essentially about a person who's kind of carefree," he says, "and they know that something might not be the best thing to do, but they're going all in with it anyway. They're just going for it, regardless of the outcome and any repercussions they might face."

If that sounds familiar, perhaps like the attitude of a man who might risk everything to drop out of school and move across the country to pursue a dream, it's no coincidence. With songs this good, it's a safe bet that a restless soul like David Luning is going to keep on traveling for a long time to come.

title: ORGONE
description:
For nearly twenty years ORGŌNE \(a universal life force, pronounced or-gōne\) has churned out gritty funk and soul recordings and toured relentlessly across the United States and Europe. Traditionally both the studio and live iterations of the band drew on a tight-knit collective of the West Coast’s finest funk and soul musicians—although founding members Sergio Rios \(guitar/engineer\) and Dan Hastie \(keyboards\) have been constant anchors. Since late 2013, Rios and Hastie have been joined by Dale Jennings \(bass\) and Sam Halterman \(drums\) to form a permanent nucleus.

ORGŌNE’s accolades are too long to list in entirety. ORGŌNE’s live show captivates audiences and packs dance floors—whether it’s on sold out headlining tours; sharing the stage with The Roots, Al Green, Sharon Jones & the Dap-Kings, and Galactic; or appearances at festivals like Bonnaroo, New Orleans Jazz Fest, High Sierra, Bear Creek, and Jam Cruise. The well-traveled band has released albums on Ubiquity, Shanachie, and Colemine Records and served as the studio band on hits like Alicia Keys’ “Teenage Love Affair” and Cee Lo Green’s Grammy-winning “Fool For You.” Critics like NPR and Jambase don’t shy away from heaping praise on a group with “irresistible funkiness and ability to transcend genre” \(LA Weekly\).

Since ORGŌNE released their album Connection on 3 Palm Records, and distributed by Colemine Records and Secretly Distribution, they have released multiple singles including their cover of “It’s My Thing”, featuring Adryon de Leon. Their second LP from 3 Palm Records was releases in 2021, Moonshadows; featuring multiple artists from the Orgone family to create a flying high blend of late 70’s California soul and funky rock.

Introduction to Asemic Writing Saturday, December 12th, 2026 - 10:00am-4:00pm$160.00 + $15.00 Materials Fee = $175.00 RegistrationClass Limited to 12 StudentsRegister now for both of Sherrie Lovler’s Workshops this weekend, and receive $20.00 off your total order! Use code SHRRLVLR-EARLYBIRD-12121326 to claim your discount!December 12th: Introduction to Asemic WritingDecember 13th: Wabi-Sabi Ink Painting: Finding Beauty in ImperfectionClass Description: Asemic writing is the creation of marks that resemble handwriting but carry no literal meaning or readable text. It is the word before words form—the voice too distant to be understood—a universal expression without country or dialect.We’ll begin with a slideshow exploring the rich history and possibilities of asemic writing, from ancient scripts and symbols to the calligraphic line and the work of contemporary artists. From there, you’ll begin your own exploration using ink, watercolor, and a variety of tools on paper.Through guided exercises and playful experimentation, we’ll explore line, gesture, rhythm, repetition, and space. You’ll discover how asemic marks can infiltrate and transform your existing artwork or become works of art in their own right.You’ll leave with a collection of new work, fresh approaches to mark-making, and a deeper trust in your own intuition and expressive voice. My intention is to guide you beyond casual scribbling toward authentic marks—marks that arise from the heart and become uniquely your own.All levels welcome.IMPORTANT: CLICK HERE FOR THE LIST OF REQUIRED MATERIALS FOR THIS CLASS. Not all materials are provided, please see the list of request materials above. If you have any questions regarding materials, please contact your instructor: sherrie@artandpoetry.com—About the Instructor: Sherrie Lovler is a painter, poet, and teacher whose work bridges Western calligraphy and the expressive spirit of Asian brush painting. With a BA in Studio Art, she has taught for several decades at international calligraphy conferences and institutions including Ghost Ranch, Northern Arizona University, and local art centers. Her paintings explore the space between writing and image. Inspired by Asian brushwork and the Japanese aesthetic of wabi-sabi, she embraces imperfection, spontaneity, and fluid mark-making. Sumi ink, gesture, color, and asemic writing become an abstract visual language. She is the author, illustrator, and designer of the award-winning book On Softer Ground. Her latest book, Distant Voices, explores art as a collaboration with nature, poetry, and unseen influences. She participates in Sonoma County Art Trails, Art at the Source, and presented a solo exhibition at Gallery Route One in Point Reyes Station in 2025. www.artandpoetry.com
