title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting
description:
Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.

Overeaters Anonymous \(OA\) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at ​Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery by practicing the Twelve Steps and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

title: Belonging to Ourselves: Understanding Trauma & Building Resilience
description:
with Pawan Bareja, PhD and Diane Poole Heller

We begin life with a child’s open heart, full of trust, innocence, and pure joy. Yet, over time, the world leaves its marks. We often arrive at our meditation cushions carrying a lifetime of hidden grief, from the lingering ache of a breakup to the quiet sorrow of a loveless childhood. To protect ourselves from this attachment trauma, we build walls that close us off from the very people we wish to love.

This daylong is an invitation to return home to the pure love that is your true nature. We do not heal in isolation; we heal together. Our nervous systems are beautifully social, wired to find safety, warmth, and co-regulation in the presence of others.

If accepting love feels foreign, you can break those protective patterns. Through guided meditations, gentle reflection, and supportive group connections, we will mend broken bonds, navigate love and conflict, and rebuild our lasting resilience.

Diane will lead a practical teaching session drawing on her background in nervous-system-informed approaches to attachment, offering an embodied complement to the day’s content.

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Saturdays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? You’ve mastered the basics, now it’s time to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

**What You’ll Learn**

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

**• The Cross Body Lead (CBL) Series:** Master both **Inside and Outside Turns**, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

**• The “I Turn – You Turn”:** A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

**• The Walk-Through:** Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

**• Footwork & Shine:** We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

**Technique & Artistry**

Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

**• The Frame:** Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

**• Upper Body Mechanics:** Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

**• Connection:** Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

**Important Details**

**• No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**• No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

**•** Please wear **non-marking shoe soles:** This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

Date & Time:

Address: 4140 Redwood Highway #8 San Rafael, CA

Note: Arrive 10 minutes before. No floor marking shoe soles allowed.

description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. Celebrate the magic of the holiday season with Bright Nights, an evening wine tasting experience set against one of Cuvaison’s most enchanting backdrops: rows and rows of estate vineyards illuminated with twinkling lights.

Offered Friday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings from November 27 through January 3, Bright Nights invites you to experience the beauty of wine country after dark as the vineyard comes alive with a warm holiday glow. From 5:00pm to 7:00pm, settle in for a cozy seasonal tasting featuring a selection of Cuvaison wines served with seasonal cheese and charcuterie pairing.

Whether you’re gathering with friends, celebrating the season, or creating a new holiday tradition, Bright Nights offers a festive and memorable way to enjoy the estate.

Experience Highlights:

·         Rows of estate vineyards illuminated with twinkling holiday lights

·         Curated wine and cheese pairings

title: Callie Watts
location: Montagne Russe Winery and Record Lounge
description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. Over time, she’s had the honor of opening for acts such as Bootsy Collins, Elvin Bishop, Huey Lewis and The News, War, Ozomatli, Bill Champlin, Booker T, and the B52s. Callie continues to perform frequently as an acoustic solo artist, focusing on developing a core audience and a buzz for her original material. Come hang out and listen at venues such as Aroma Roasters, Rincon Valley Tap Room and Bottle Shop, and Hopmonk Tavern.

title: Winter Wonder Lantern Walks
description:
Celebrate the beauty and quiet magic of the season during Winter Wonder Lantern Walks, a festive after-dark experience at Sonoma Botanical Garden. Guided along the route by Garden staff and volunteers, guests will stroll through the winter landscape carrying glowing lanterns, discovering softly shadowed pathways, towering trees, and the peaceful stillness of the Garden beneath the night sky. Rather than a traditional docent-led tour, this experience is designed as a peaceful and immersive opportunity to enjoy the rare experience of walking through the Garden after hours and after dark. Along the way, enjoy moments of reflection, seasonal ambiance, and the simple joy of gathering outdoors during the holiday season.

The evening begins with hot cocoa, spiced cider, wine tasting and cookies from 5:30–6:00 p.m., followed by a brief welcome and lantern walk orientation before departing together for a guided walk through the Garden.

Winter Wonder Lantern Walks are a seasonal fundraiser that will support the Garden’s programs, collections, and conservation efforts. PLEASE READ the important accessibility and experience information, along with the registration and cancellation policy below before purchasing tickets.

title: Fright Night with Cameron Pierce & David Agranoff
description:
Join us at 6 pm on SATURDAY, DECEMBER 12 for another FRIGHT NIGHT author event with readings, Q&A, and signings.

This time we're featuring CAMERON PIERCE in conversation with DAVID AGRANOFF for an evening of bizarro literature. With Ross E. Lockhart moderating, it's sure to be a fascinating discussion.

Cameron Pierce's new novel *Most Things Haven't Worked Out*, just published by CLASH Books, is a coming of age story about the painful pursuit of love, fortune, and fame reading like an optimistic Jesus' Son for a new generation. Told through a series of follies, Pierce presents a journey of finding agency from someone who doesn't have an inkling of what they want out of life.

David Agranoff's latest CLASH novel, *The Last Night to Kill Nazis*, is an emotional rollercoaster of adventure, terror and revenge that explores one of the world's most evil events through the lens of a horror novel. An entertaining and enlightening novel that is *Inglorious Basterds* meets *Dracula*. Watch for the sequel *The Next Night to Kill Nazis* coming in January!

location: Spreckels Center for the Performing Arts - Bette Condiotti Experimental Theatre
description:
This holiday season, Spreckels Theatre Company offers a heartwarming alternative to traditional seasonal fare with *Rooted*, a story about the messy, fierce love that keeps us grounded. An intelligent, gentle comedy by Deborah Zoe Laufer, *Rooted* plays Nov. 27 – Dec.13!

Emery is perfectly content living in her beloved treehouse, completely isolated from the world, communing with her plants. Meanwhile, down on the ground, her sister Hazel is thoroughly miserable, slaving away at a dead-end diner job just to survive and financially support Emery’s eccentric lifestyle. Looking on from the sidelines, Luanne is yearning for something, anything to bring true meaning into her life.

﻿The sisters' fragile ecosystem is completely upended when Emery’s YouTube videos documenting her plant experiments unexpectedly go viral. Almost overnight, her digital musings accidentally incite a full-blown CULT(!). As throngs of devoted truth-seekers congregate below the treehouse, the lives of all three women are plunged into chaos, compelling each woman to choose their own path and find their bliss.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

Use code SHRRLVLR-EARLYBIRD-12121326 to claim your discount!December 12th: Introduction to Asemic WritingDecember 13th: Wabi-Sabi Ink Painting: Finding Beauty in ImperfectionClass Description: Step into a creative space where intuition leads and imperfection becomes beauty. This immersive workshop explores abstract painting through both Eastern and Western perspectives, blending meditation, movement, and mark-making to create expressive, finished paintings.Rooted in the Japanese aesthetic of wabi-sabi, we’ll release the desire for perfection and welcome the unexpected. Discover the quiet magic that happens when ink meets water, gestures emerge without planning, and the body and breath guide the brush.We’ll begin with gentle centering and meditation, preparing you to work from the heart and engage your whole body in the creative process. You’ll practice painting the ensō—the Zen circle expressing wholeness, presence, movement, and stillness. Using Asian brushes, ink, and watercolor on paper, you will create calligraphic paintings with layered accents that bring depth, atmosphere, and emotion to your work.Through guided exercises and open-ended exploration, you’ll learn to trust your intuition, loosen up, and respond to what unfolds. You’ll leave with a collection of expressive paintings and new ways to bring spontaneity and freedom into your artwork.All levels welcome.IMPORTANT: CLICK HERE FOR THE LIST OF REQUIRED MATERIALS FOR THIS CLASS. Not all materials are provided, please see the list of request materials above. If you have any questions regarding materials, please contact your instructor: sherrie@artandpoetry.com—About the Instructor: Sherrie Lovler is a painter, poet, and teacher whose work bridges Western calligraphy and the expressive spirit of Asian brush painting. With a BA in Studio Art, she has taught for several decades at international calligraphy conferences and institutions including Ghost Ranch, Northern Arizona University, and local art centers. Her paintings explore the space between writing and image. Inspired by Asian brushwork and the Japanese aesthetic of wabi-sabi, she embraces imperfection, spontaneity, and fluid mark-making. Sumi ink, gesture, color, and asemic writing become an abstract visual language. She is the author, illustrator, and designer of the award-winning book On Softer Ground. Her latest book, Distant Voices, explores art as a collaboration with nature, poetry, and unseen influences. She participates in Sonoma County Art Trails, Art at the Source, and presented a solo exhibition at Gallery Route One in Point Reyes Station in 2025. www.artandpoetry.com

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. Set in 1904 on the eve of the St. Louis World’s Fair, the story follows the Smith family through a year of romance, humor, and unexpected change. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. LOUIS is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Tams-Witmark LLC. concordtheatricals.com

This holiday season, Spreckels Theatre Company offers a heartwarming alternative to traditional seasonal fare with *Rooted*, a story about the messy, fierce love that keeps us grounded. An intelligent, gentle comedy by Deborah Zoe Laufer, *Rooted* plays Nov. 27 – Dec.13!

Emery is perfectly content living in her beloved treehouse, completely isolated from the world, communing with her plants. Meanwhile, down on the ground, her sister Hazel is thoroughly miserable, slaving away at a dead-end diner job just to survive and financially support Emery’s eccentric lifestyle. Looking on from the sidelines, Luanne is yearning for something, anything to bring true meaning into her life.

﻿The sisters' fragile ecosystem is completely upended when Emery’s YouTube videos documenting her plant experiments unexpectedly go viral. Almost overnight, her digital musings accidentally incite a full-blown CULT(!). As throngs of devoted truth-seekers congregate below the treehouse, the lives of all three women are plunged into chaos, compelling each woman to choose their own path and find their bliss.

title: Focus Night: Geminids Meteor Shower
description: Move over, summer Perseids. December's Geminid shower is considered the best and most reliable meteor shower of the year. Under dark clear skies, counts can reach 50-100 per hour or more on peak night. But this is only one of many factors that set these meteors apart from all other showers. Their speed and composition create meteors that flare low in the atmosphere, are easier to spot, and leave bright, often yellow, trails. This is one of the very few showers visible all night long. What causes this dazzling display and why does it occur at this time of year? Come learn about these unique meteors, their unusual history, and their mysterious origin. This Focus Night equips you for a Geminid ”peak” experience. Unlike planets that can hang around for months, a meteor shower is only visible over a short period of time. Highest counts will occur later in the night and into the early morning hours. You will learn about different kinds of showers, how best to view them, and how to understand what you are seeing. You’ll also discover factors that influence meteor counts and how to optimize your viewing. Plan to be in the classroom by 6:55PM to ensure you have a good seat. Program begins promptly at 7:00PM . Sales are limited to 40 guests so we can provide a more personal experience. Allow generous time to arrive and park. Please visit https://rfo.simpletix.com for important information and to buy tickets. You MUST have a ticket to attend this event; tickets will not be sold at the door. Cost includes the Sugarloaf Ridge State Park parking fee. Please note that tickets are non-refundable and cannot be used for future events.RFO is operated by the Valley of the Moon Observatory Association, a 501(3)(c) nonprofit organization. All proceeds go toward maintaining this beloved Sonoma County institution.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

title: Give 'Em the Axe! Ladies Night at the Range in Santa Rosa
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
Join us for an axe-throwing session to blow off some steam. I'm super excited to be able to offer a ladies' Axe-throwing night in Santa Rosa. If you've ever had a curiosity about this fun activity, this is your chance to find out more!

We have reserved a group spot with the indoor range on a Wednesday night. It will consist of an introductory lesson, and then we all get to practice taking turns. Everyone will get ample time to practice, as they have many lanes.

This event is focused on a less-competitive, relaxed, and entertaining atmosphere. All skill levels are encouraged. All equipment and targets are provided by them, and we will probably get about 1 to 2 hours to enjoy ourselves.

I encourage everyone to bring a bottle of wine or a snack to share with the rest of the group (We usually end up with a lovely charcuterie and wine spread for everyone to enjoy).

There are 10 spots available, guests welcome. The ladies' group lesson and event is $31 per person, with $6 prepaid via Paypal and $25 paid to the range.

Please only RSVP 'Yes' if you are able to make it, hostess Daima Phipps will be collecting a $6 fee via Paypal to hold your spot. Paypal/Meetup should lead you to make your payment after you RSVP 'Yes'.

Closed-toed shoes are recommended.

There is an attendance policy for all our events: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

Cheers, and hope to see you there!

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Young, Gifted, and Black - Art Submissions Due
description: Young, Gifted, and Black: Art by Black Students at SRJC is an upcoming exhibition at the SRJC Multicultural Museum celebrating the creativity and artistic voices of Black students across campus. Created in recognition of Black History Month, the exhibition provides a dedicated space for Black student artists to have their work seen, valued, and celebrated by the SRJC community.  Black students are invited to submit original artwork in any medium or theme, including visual art, poetry, and other forms of creative writing. Artwork does not need to focus on Black identity or the Black experience—the exhibition celebrates the breadth of Black creativity and the individuality of each participating artist.  The exhibition will be on display in the ground floor library display cases from the beginning of the Spring 2027 semester through Spring Break. Students interested in participating must drop off their work at the SRJC Multicultural Museum by December 18, 2026.Learn more about the museum on the SRJC Multicultural Museum website. Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke (option 1)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
A modern day Christian tradwife Natalie decides with her husband to take the family to live in a farmhouse, grow their own food, raise chickens and a cow, and raise/home school their ever-increasing brood without modern influences. However -- mom is also a social media influencer who videos everything... except the nannies and farmworkers behind the scenes. She wakes up one day and she and some version of her family are in a real farmhouse (with no helpers) in 1855! How to get out of this nightmare/delusion/time travel?

"I found it to be a realy page turner--couldn't put it down. I definitely think that we should read this for our group. It's so unusual and I think it would provide fodder for very interesting discussion." - Nancy R.

"For the life of me, I can’t figure out why I kept reading this book given that most of the characters in it are deplorable. But I sure kept reading it. And then when I finished it, I wondered what kind of a person could write such a book and I was surprised when I listened to the interview that the author is actually full-fledged human being with a heart and a sense of humor. To me, that the sign of someone with tremendous craft. There are many topics in this book that I think would be a wealth for us to discuss: The double lives of social media influencers, Tradwife vs Girlboss, can we go back into the way that used to be. I suspect the reason this book is so hot because it’s so topical." - Lucinda

"It took me a bit to get into (I was just so annoyed at the beginning:) but after things began to develop, I was hooked. A lot to discuss - although it may be tough to separate out discussion on the book itself and the real-world implications!" - Debra

"[Why You Should Read ‘Yesteryear’ Now](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/10/briefing/yesteryear-caro-claire-burke.html?unlocked_article_code=1.01A.Gak9.SZGpJviEJq74&smid=url-share)" - NY Times

"‘[Yesteryear’ is this summer’s must-discuss book. We have questions.](https://www.washingtonpost.com/style/interactive/2026/06/18/yesteryear-is-this-summers-must-read-book-let-discuss/)" - Washington Post:

This is a hands-on make and take class where you will make at least five items including a bookmark, a greeting card, a fridge magnet and an ornament. To register for this workshop, please contact Jan at: mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com

Creating note cards from pressed flowers has been Jan’s hobby for 25 years, though she has no formal art training. She utilizes color,
shape and texture on fine quality paper, each card uniquely handmade. Jan’s home in Sebastopol is her studio: the dining room table is her workshop, the kitchen cupboards storing boxes and trays of flowers. She buys card stock by the thousand and picks blooms from her garden and other public places. Her family is used to me saying, “could we stop for just a few minutes so I can gather some… ”

It is a wonderful way of life.

Sips and Stars ~ an evening of fine wine and cosmic wonder.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

Step into a transformative space where for women to delve into **self-exploration, art therapy**, and mindfulness come together to nurture your inner wisdom. Students of all walks of life, abilities, and experience writing poetry, or spoken word poetry, are encouraged to join. Students will engage in a freewrite, poetry reading, discussion, and structured writing with a voluntary shareout. After the one hour workshop, Poetry Lives! will act as an Open Mic night open to all to read their completed, or previously completed, poems. To register for the Open Mic only, please select Open Mic Only below! All workshop registrations include registration to the open mic as well. Poetry Lives! is a monthly poetry workshop and open mic series that aims to create a space for anyone and everyone to come, learn more about poetic craft, and share their poetry. The event starts with a facilitated hour-long workshop dedicated to learning craft elements, discovering new poets, and generating new work. Once the workshop concludes, we will hold a hosted open mic for anyone who wishes to share. It is not mandatory to participate in the workshop to be a part of the open mic or vice versa. This event is all ages, but that doesn't necessarily mean family-friendly, as poets are known to cover mature and adult topics from time to time. About the Poet: Jordan Ranft (He/Him) is a writer and therapist from Northern California. He has been nominated for a Pushcart and Best of the Net. His poetry has been published or is forthcoming in Boulevard Magazine, Frontier Poetry, Poetry Online, Bear Review, Iron Horse Literary Review, and elsewhere. His first chapbook, Said the Worms, was published in June 2023 by Wrong Publishing. He is currently working on a second chapbook and full-length collection. Wednesday, Ongoing

Location: Santa Rosa Store

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke (option 2)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
A modern day Christian tradwife Natalie decides with her husband to take the family to live in a farmhouse, grow their own food, raise chickens and a cow, and raise/home school their ever-increasing brood without modern influences. However -- mom is also a social media influencer who videos everything... except the nannies and farmworkers behind the scenes. She wakes up one day and she and some version of her family are in a real farmhouse (with no helpers) in 1855! How to get out of this nightmare/delusion/time travel?

"I found it to be a realy page turner--couldn't put it down. I definitely think that we should read this for our group. It's so unusual and I think it would provide fodder for very interesting discussion." - Nancy R.

"For the life of me, I can’t figure out why I kept reading this book given that most of the characters in it are deplorable. But I sure kept reading it. And then when I finished it, I wondered what kind of a person could write such a book and I was surprised when I listened to the interview that the author is actually full-fledged human being with a heart and a sense of humor. To me, that the sign of someone with tremendous craft. There are many topics in this book that I think would be a wealth for us to discuss: The double lives of social media influencers, Tradwife vs Girlboss, can we go back into the way that used to be. I suspect the reason this book is so hot because it’s so topical." - Lucinda

"It took me a bit to get into (I was just so annoyed at the beginning:) but after things began to develop, I was hooked. A lot to discuss - although it may be tough to separate out discussion on the book itself and the real-world implications!" - Debra

"[Why You Should Read ‘Yesteryear’ Now](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/10/briefing/yesteryear-caro-claire-burke.html?unlocked_article_code=1.01A.Gak9.SZGpJviEJq74&smid=url-share)" - NY Times

"‘[Yesteryear’ is this summer’s must-discuss book. We have questions.](https://www.washingtonpost.com/style/interactive/2026/06/18/yesteryear-is-this-summers-must-read-book-let-discuss/)" - Washington Post

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

description:
Sips and Stars ~ an evening of fine wine and cosmic wonder.

Join us for a magical night under the stars at the Robert Ferguson Observatory! Our Sips & Stars event blends the beauty of the night sky with the elegance of Sonoma County wine. Enjoy a curated tasting experience hosted by a local winery, while taking in breathtaking views of the cosmos through our powerful telescopes.

Whether you’re a wine lover, stargazer, or simply looking for a unique evening out in Sonoma Valley, Sips & Stars promises an unforgettable experience where earthly pleasures meet celestial beauty.

Guests must be 21 or older to attend and each registration includes two drink tickets. Proceeds support the Robert Ferguson Observatory’s public education programs.

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes

  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors

  * Proper brush care and maintenance

They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

location: Out West Garage, 321 Second Street, Petaluma, 94952, United States
description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

Let's make beautiful art together!

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: FULL Weave Your Own Ribs Style Foraging Basket (Berkeley)
John of John by Douglas Stuart (option 1)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
*Publisher's description*: A vivid, moving novel following a young man returning to his Hebridean island home, a portrait of a father's expectations and a son's desires.

Out of money and with little to show for his art school education, John-Calum Macleod takes the ferry back home to the Isle of Harris in the Outer Hebrides to find that little has changed except for him. He returns to the windswept croft and the two pillars of his childhood: his father John, a sheep farmer, tweed weaver, and lay preacher in the local Presbyterian church, and his maternal grandmother Ella, a profanity-loving Glaswegian whose steady warmth helped Cal weather the sudden departure of his mother.

Cal privately wonders if any lonely men might be found on the barren hillsides of home, while John is dismayed by his son's long hair, strange clothes, and seeming unwillingness to be Saved. But Cal isn't the only one who is keeping secrets. As lambing season turns to shearing season, the threads holding together the community together become increasingly frayed, and nothing will remain as it was before. *John of John* is a singular novel about duty, passion, and the transformative power of the truth.

*From our members*:

Mac: "a must-read for our Novel Lovers discussions. It contains beautiful, accurate descriptions of the harsh sere landscape in the Outer Hebrides where I’ve visited. It’s filled with secrets, many revealed and others not. Stuart dishes up human hope and despair in equal measure. Having dwelt on very different islands with small face-to-face communities like those on Harris and Lewis, the novel reflects life in many other places besides the far west of Scotland."

Matthew: "I did appreciate *John of John* and greatly admire Douglas Stuart's thoughtful writing. Sheep farming on a remote Scottish isle is a world so removed. It's very much an internal dialogue with the handful of characters, with a number ancillary family members and neighbors. I finished the book several weeks ago and it's stayed with me."

Ma'ayan: "I LOVED it all the way through. It broke my heart but also gave me hope. I laughed out loud at certain parts, too. The writing is so visceral. This one really stole my heart."

Joan: "So much in this book. It's about finding/denying/finding one's true self; keeping family secrets and secrets kept from family; passion and denial of passion; staying upright when family, religion, and the hardscrabble life of sheep farming on a Scottish island beat you down. Some books just get to you. This one gets to me."
