title: Voyage Hot Club
description:
Django meets French Chanson
Award-winning violinist
Eva Slongo
, guitarist
Jimmy Grant
and Double bassist
Simon Planting
present an intimate and swinging duo rooted in the gypsy jazz tradition of
Django Reinhardt
and
Stéphane Grappelli
. Their music draws equally from European jazz, Eastern European folk influences, and classic vocal jazz, resulting in a sound that feels both timeless and accessible to modern audiences.
Their repertoire includes French chanson, swing standards, and original arrangements that evoke travel, nostalgia, and joy. Whether presented in a listening-room jazz club, concert hall, or outdoor summer series, Eva and Jimmy offer a warm, dynamic performance that emphasizes groove, melody, and connection.
Tickets for this event are $33 GA, $28 for OCA members. Doors open at 6:30 PM, refreshments available. Art Gallery open during intermission Contact us to request ADA seating,
info@occidentalcenterforthearts.org
Get Tickets
About the performers:
Jimmy Grant,
hailing from Northern California, discovered Django Reinhardt's vibrant sounds while touring with his dad’s bluegrass band. His unique style, shaped by influences like Bach and Joe Pass, was honed under the mentorship of guitarists Jim Nichols and Howard Alden.
Jimmy has performed with renowned artists such as David Grisman, Gonzalo Bergara, and many more showcasing his talent at prestigious events like Djangofest Northwest and The New York Hot Jazz Festival, as well as venues throughout the US & Europe.
As an educator, he teaches across the U.S. and hosts "Camp Django" in Ashland, OR. He contributes to "Gypsy Jazz Secrets Magazine" and has recorded two albums. His original composition "Insomnia" was a finalist in the John Lennon Songwriting Competition.
Eva Slongo
was born in Switzerland to a family of classical musicians. She first trained as a professional classical violinist.
One day, by chance, she tried to improvise with musicians in a bar; she felt such euphoria that she spent a sleepless night … It was then that she decided to do everything she could to practice improvisation on the violin.
After her classical diplomas, she changed direction and started from scratch … She studied jazz violin with Pierre Blanchard in Lausanne, then with Didier Lockwood in Paris, where she decided to stay and live for music. She also practiced improvisation on vocals, which led her to create her very noticeable unique color: improvising on the violin and scatting simultaneously.
In Paris, Eva Slongo met renowned musicians from the world of gypsy jazz with whom she shared the stage: Biréli Lagrène, Wawau Adler, Sébastien Giniaux, Ninine Garcia, and many others …
In 2011, she won the Prize for Best Improvisation at the Stéphane Grappelli International Violin Competition sponsored by Didier Lockwood. In 2016, she obtained the 2nd prize of the Golden Jazz Trophy with her quartet.
After all these years of experience, she was led to give masterclasses internationally. She needed to share more of her learning of the jazz violin, but struggled to find the time and method to do so. Her first pregnancy forced her to slow down concerts… but it led her to do what she would never have imagined: create a new educational concept on the internet, the blog “Learn Jazz Violin” which has become the 1st Google search result in French jazz violin, and finally a method “The new way to learn jazz violin.”
Eva Slongo’s new album “Souffle” was recorded in collaboration with pianist Giovanni Mirabassi, with whom she shares the stage regularly.
Dutch double bassist
Simon Planting
studied classical bass at the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra and jazz at the Sweelinck Conservatory in Amsterdam. Now based near San Francisco, he has performed internationally with artists including Mathilde Santing, Fapy Lafertin, Jimmy Rosenberg, Stephane Wrembel, and John Jorgenson, and is a fixture on the Djangofest circuit.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting in 2026, we ask that every attending member pay a $2 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

title: John of John by Douglas Stuart (option 2)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
*Publisher's description*: A vivid, moving novel following a young man returning to his Hebridean island home, a portrait of a father's expectations and a son's desires.

Out of money and with little to show for his art school education, John-Calum Macleod takes the ferry back home to the Isle of Harris in the Outer Hebrides to find that little has changed except for him. He returns to the windswept croft and the two pillars of his childhood: his father John, a sheep farmer, tweed weaver, and lay preacher in the local Presbyterian church, and his maternal grandmother Ella, a profanity-loving Glaswegian whose steady warmth helped Cal weather the sudden departure of his mother.

Cal privately wonders if any lonely men might be found on the barren hillsides of home, while John is dismayed by his son's long hair, strange clothes, and seeming unwillingness to be Saved. But Cal isn't the only one who is keeping secrets. As lambing season turns to shearing season, the threads holding together the community together become increasingly frayed, and nothing will remain as it was before. *John of John* is a singular novel about duty, passion, and the transformative power of the truth.

*From our members*:

Mac: "a must-read for our Novel Lovers discussions. It contains beautiful, accurate descriptions of the harsh sere landscape in the Outer Hebrides where I’ve visited. It’s filled with secrets, many revealed and others not. Stuart dishes up human hope and despair in equal measure. Having dwelt on very different islands with small face-to-face communities like those on Harris and Lewis, the novel reflects life in many other places besides the far west of Scotland."

Matthew: "I did appreciate *John of John* and greatly admire Douglas Stuart's thoughtful writing. Sheep farming on a remote Scottish isle is a world so removed. It's very much an internal dialogue with the handful of characters, with a number ancillary family members and neighbors. I finished the book several weeks ago and it's stayed with me."

Ma'ayan: "I LOVED it all the way through. It broke my heart but also gave me hope. I laughed out loud at certain parts, too. The writing is so visceral. This one really stole my heart."

Joan: "So much in this book. It's about finding/denying/finding one's true self; keeping family secrets and secrets kept from family; passion and denial of passion; staying upright when family, religion, and the hardscrabble life of sheep farming on a Scottish island beat you down. Some books just get to you. This one gets to me."

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: Deep Sky Astrophotography Processing class (class 1 of 3)
description: Have you ever admired amazing deep sky astrophotography images and wondered if you could ever create similar images?  Now you can!   With raw data provided from the telescopes at the Robert Ferguson Observatory, in this class series of three sessions you will have the opportunity to learn how to process and edit your own beautiful deep sky images. Please note, this workshop is meant as a 3-class series. It is highly recommended to purchase tickets for all three days.Please note, this is a virtual class. A Zoom link will be sent to participants prior to the class. What you will learn in this class:- The fundamentals of Deep Sky Astrophotography- An overview of image capture techniques (a dedicated, hands-on class on Deep sky image capture using your own equipment will be held later in Spring 2025)- Robert Ferguson Observatory Image capture techniques - how we captured the data that will be used in this class.- An overview of image processing techniques- An introduction to Siril, a free and open-source Astronomical Image Processing Program- A hands-on session where you will process data collected at the Robert Ferguson Observatory - A wrap-up session where you will have the opportunity to share and discuss your images with other class attendees Class Prerequisites:- A computer newer than 5-years old (the newer the better), loaded with the latest operating system- At least 8MB of RAM (more is better)- At least 50GB of free disk space (preferably a solid-state disk drive.  More storage is better)- Familiarity with creating directories, moving files between folders, setting folder and file permissions, and accessing cloud drives.Get more information and purchase tickets at rfo.simpletix.com.

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

description: Have you ever admired amazing deep sky astrophotography images and wondered if you could ever create similar images?  Now you can!   With raw data provided from the telescopes at the Robert Ferguson Observatory, in this class series of three sessions you will have the opportunity to learn how to process and edit your own beautiful deep sky images. Please note, this workshop is meant as a 3-class series. A Zoom link will be sent to participants prior to the class. What you will learn in this class:- The fundamentals of Deep Sky Astrophotography- An overview of image capture techniques (a dedicated, hands-on class on Deep sky image capture using your own equipment will be held later in Spring 2025)- Robert Ferguson Observatory Image capture techniques - how we captured the data that will be used in this class.- An overview of image processing techniques- An introduction to Siril, a free and open-source Astronomical Image Processing Program- A hands-on session where you will process data collected at the Robert Ferguson Observatory - A wrap-up session where you will have the opportunity to share and discuss your images with other class attendees Class Prerequisites:- A computer newer than 5-years old (the newer the better), loaded with the latest operating system- At least 8MB of RAM (more is better)- At least 50GB of free disk space (preferably a solid-state disk drive.  More storage is better)- Familiarity with creating directories, moving files between folders, setting folder and file permissions, and accessing cloud drives.Get more information and purchase tickets at rfo.simpletix.com.

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

description:

description:

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.
